description: Total number of sequencing reads contained in this artifact. For FASTQ files, represents raw read count; for BAM/CRAM files, represents total aligned and unaligned reads. Used for QC assessment, yield reporting, and billing calculations.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; LabVantage LIMS; CLIA

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this genomic artifact record in the registry, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Tracks record modifications for audit trail compliance and change detection in downstream pipelines.
reference: ISO 8601; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; GxP; HIPAA Security Rule

description: Regulatory use classification of the artifact indicating its intended application context. 'RUO' (Research Use Only) — not for diagnostic use; 'IVD' (In Vitro Diagnostic) — cleared/approved for clinical diagnostics; 'LDT' (Laboratory Developed Test) — validated in-house clinical test; 'clinical' — used in clinical reporting; 'research' — used in research studies; 'internal_qc' — internal quality control purposes.
reference: FDA (U.S. Food and Drug Administration) IVD Regulations; IVDR (EU In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation 2017/746); CLIA; CAP

description: Total number of genomic variants (SNPs, indels, CNVs, SVs) recorded in this artifact for VCF and gVCF file types. Provides a high-level QC indicator and enables rapid assessment of variant calling yield without parsing the full VCF file.

Unique surrogate identifier for each BAM/CRAM alignment result record produced by a bioinformatics pipeline run. Primary key for this entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — this entity represents a discrete computational event (alignment job output) with its own lifecycle, QC status, and lineage.

Reference to the bioinformatics pipeline run that produced this alignment result. Links the alignment output back to the specific pipeline execution context, enabling full data lineage from raw FASTQ input to aligned output. Satisfies PARTY_REFERENCE / RESOURCE_REFERENCE category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: ISO 15189; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines; ALCOA+ Principles

description: Identifier of the sequencing Flow Cell used to generate the raw reads for this alignment. The Flow Cell is the consumable cartridge on which sequencing chemistry occurs. Traceability to the flow cell enables investigation of batch-level sequencing failures, reagent lot issues, and instrument performance trends.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; LabVantage LIMS; ISO 15189 Traceability Requirements

description: Reference to the reference genome assembly used for alignment (e.g., GRCh38/hg38, T2T-CHM13). The choice of reference genome directly impacts variant calling accuracy and clinical interpretation; this linkage is mandatory for reproducibility and regulatory traceability.
reference: NCBI RefSeq; Genome Reference Consortium (GRC); NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Alignment QC results require qualified bioinformatician review before downstream variant calling, especially for clinical/GxP pipelines. Required for quality gate enforcement, personnel qualification

Reference to the biological sample that was sequenced and aligned. Establishes traceability from the alignment result back to the originating sample, supporting clinical reporting, regulatory audit, and downstream variant analysis workflows.
reference: ISO 15189; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP Accreditation Standards

Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Alignment QC metrics (coverage depth, mapping rate) establish analytical validity in regulatory submissions for NGS-based IVDs. New attribute links alignment results to submissions for performance cla

Name of the alignment software tool used to produce this result (e.g., BWA-MEM, BWA-MEM2, DRAGEN, STAR, Bowtie2, minimap2). The choice of aligner affects sensitivity, specificity, and computational cost. Required for reproducibility and regulatory method validation documentation.
reference: ISO 15189; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; Bioinformatics Pipeline Validation Guidelines

description: Semantic version string of the aligner tool used (e.g., 0.7.17, 2.2.1). Version tracking is mandatory for bioinformatics method validation, regulatory submissions (FDA, EMA), and reproducibility of clinical genomic results. A version change may require re-validation under ISO 15189 and CLIA.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 15189; ICH E6 GCP; GxP Software Validation

description: The date and time at which the alignment job completed and the BAM/CRAM output file was finalized. Represents the principal real-world business event time for this record. Used for Turnaround Time (TAT) calculations, SLA monitoring, and pipeline performance analytics. Satisfies BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category.
reference: ISO 15189; CLIA TAT Requirements; GxP ALCOA+ Principles

description: Percentage of reads flagged as chimeric (reads where the two ends map to different chromosomes or distant genomic locations). Elevated chimeric rates indicate library preparation artifacts, structural variant signals, or sequencing errors. Monitored as a QC metric in clinical WGS and structural variant detection workflows.
reference: STAR Aligner Documentation; Picard CollectAlignmentSummaryMetrics; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines

description: Compute infrastructure platform on which the alignment job was executed: AWS (Amazon Web Services), on-premise High-Performance Computing (HPC) cluster, Azure, GCP, or Illumina DRAGEN server. Required for cost allocation, performance benchmarking, and infrastructure capacity planning.
reference: AWS Well-Architected Framework; ISO 27001; GxP Cloud Computing Guidelines (EMA/ISPE)

description: Wall-clock time in seconds taken to complete the alignment job from job start to job completion. Used for pipeline performance monitoring, SLA compliance tracking, HPC/cloud resource optimization, and cost modeling. Enables identification of performance regressions across aligner versions or reference genome builds.
reference: AWS Cost Management; HPC Job Scheduler Logs; GxP Computerized Systems Validation

description: Percentage of target bases covered at ≥20% of the mean coverage depth, measuring the uniformity of sequencing coverage across the target region. High uniformity indicates consistent library preparation and sequencing performance. Low uniformity may indicate GC bias or capture inefficiency in WES/panel assays.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub QC Metrics; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines

description: Number of CPU cores allocated and used for the alignment job. Together with compute_runtime_seconds and memory_used_gb, enables accurate cloud compute cost attribution per alignment result and supports capacity planning for HPC/AWS infrastructure.
reference: AWS Cost Management; HPC Resource Management Standards

description: The date and time when this alignment result record was first ingested into the Silver Layer data lakehouse. Distinct from alignment_timestamp (job completion time). Used for data lineage, audit trails, and ETL monitoring. Satisfies RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.
reference: GxP ALCOA+ Principles; ISO 27001; SOX Section 404

description: Percentage of mapped reads flagged as PCR or optical duplicates (duplicate_reads / mapped_reads × 100). High duplicate rates reduce effective coverage depth and can introduce variant calling bias. Typically assessed using Picard MarkDuplicates or equivalent. Threshold violations trigger QC warning or failure.
reference: Picard Tools Documentation; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines; ISO 15189

description: Percentage of guanine (G) and cytosine (C) bases in the aligned reads. GC content deviating significantly from the expected genomic average (~41% for human) indicates GC bias in library preparation or PCR amplification, which can cause uneven coverage and affect Copy Number Variation (CNV) analysis accuracy.
reference: FastQC Quality Control Tool; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

description: Standard deviation of the insert size distribution in base pairs. A narrow distribution indicates consistent library preparation; a wide distribution may indicate mixed fragment populations or library quality issues. Used alongside median_insert_size_bp for comprehensive library QC assessment.
reference: Picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics; Illumina Library Preparation QC Standards

description: Regulatory intended use classification for this alignment result: Research Use Only (RUO), In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD), Laboratory Developed Test (LDT), clinical research, agricultural genomics, or companion diagnostic. Determines applicable regulatory framework (FDA, IVDR, CLIA) and data handling requirements including PHI/HIPAA obligations.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 820; EU IVDR 2017/746; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; HIPAA 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this alignment result is a reanalysis of a previously aligned sample (True) or an original first-pass alignment (False). Reanalyses may be triggered by reference genome updates, aligner version upgrades, QC failures, or clinical reinterpretation requests. Supports data lineage and version management.
reference: GxP Data Integrity Guidelines; ISO 15189; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Number of sequencing reads that successfully mapped to the reference genome. Together with total_reads, this is used to compute the mapping rate. Low mapped read counts may indicate sample contamination, library preparation failure, or reference genome mismatch.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub QC Metrics; SAMtools Flagstat Specification

description: Percentage of total reads that successfully mapped to the reference genome (mapped_reads / total_reads × 100). A primary alignment QC metric; typical acceptable thresholds are ≥90% for human WGS. Values below threshold trigger QC failure and potential re-sequencing.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub QC Metrics; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines; ISO 15189

description: Mean Phred Score across all bases in the aligned reads. The Phred Score is a logarithmic measure of base call accuracy (Q30 = 99.9% accuracy). A key sequencing run quality metric; Q30 ≥ 80% is a standard threshold for clinical-grade sequencing. Directly impacts variant calling sensitivity and specificity.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub QC Metrics; Phred Quality Score Standard (Ewing & Green 1998); ISO 15189

description: Average number of sequencing reads covering each base position in the target region or genome (Coverage Depth). Expressed as a fold value (e.g., 30×, 100×). A fundamental QC metric determining the statistical power for variant detection; minimum thresholds vary by application (e.g., 30× for WGS, 100× for somatic panels).
reference: ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; ISO 15189; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Median length of the DNA fragment insert in base pairs (bp) as measured from the aligned paired-end reads. Insert size distribution is a key library preparation QC metric; unexpected values indicate library degradation, adapter contamination, or incorrect size selection. Affects read overlap and variant calling accuracy.
reference: Picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics; Illumina Library Preparation QC Standards

description: Peak memory (RAM) consumed in gigabytes during the alignment job execution. Memory usage varies significantly by aligner (e.g., BWA-MEM2 requires ~60 GB for human WGS). Used for cloud instance type selection, cost optimization, and pipeline resource configuration management.
reference: AWS Cost Management; HPC Resource Management Standards; Bioinformatics Pipeline Optimization Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Percentage of Bases at ≥10× Coverage Depth
description: Percentage of target bases covered at a minimum depth of 10× reads. A standard coverage adequacy metric used in clinical genomics reporting to confirm that the majority of the target region has sufficient depth for reliable variant calling. Commonly reported in clinical assay validation and CAP/CLIA compliance.
reference: CAP Accreditation Standards; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Percentage of Bases at ≥30× Coverage Depth
description: Percentage of target bases covered at a minimum depth of 30× reads. The 30× threshold is the standard minimum for clinical Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) and is required by many regulatory and accreditation bodies. Distinct from pct_bases_above_10x as it represents a higher stringency clinical threshold.
reference: ACMG/AMP WGS Guidelines; CAP Accreditation Standards; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

business_glossary_term: Percentage of Bases with Phred Score ≥Q30
description: Percentage of sequenced bases with a Phred Score of 30 or higher (≥Q30), indicating ≥99.9% base call accuracy. The Q30 percentage is the primary sequencing run quality KPI reported by Illumina instruments and BaseSpace. Minimum thresholds (typically ≥75–80%) are defined in clinical assay SOPs and regulatory submissions.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; Phred Quality Score Standard; FDA IVD Submission Guidelines; ISO 15189

description: Percentage of read pairs where both reads mapped to the reference genome in the expected orientation and within the expected insert size range. Low properly paired rates indicate library preparation issues, adapter contamination, or reference genome incompatibility. A standard SAMtools flagstat metric.
reference: SAMtools Flagstat Specification; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub QC Metrics; ISO 15189

description: Free-text notes entered by a bioinformatics scientist or QC reviewer during manual review of this alignment result. Captures the rationale for QC status overrides, observations about anomalous metrics, or instructions for downstream processing. Required for GxP audit trail and CLIA/CAP documentation.
reference: GxP ALCOA+ Principles; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP Accreditation Standards; ISO 15189

description: Overall Quality Control (QC) pass/fail/warning determination for this alignment result based on evaluation of all QC metrics against defined thresholds. Drives downstream workflow routing: pass results proceed to variant calling; fail results trigger re-sequencing or sample rejection. Satisfies LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.
reference: ISO 15189; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP Accreditation Standards; GxP Data Integrity

description: Length of sequencing reads in base pairs (e.g., 150 bp for standard Illumina short-read, 10,000+ bp for long-read platforms). Read length affects alignment accuracy, variant detection capability (especially for structural variants and repeat regions), and computational resource requirements.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines

description: Human-readable label of the reference genome assembly build used for alignment (e.g., GRCh38/hg38, T2T-CHM13). Stored denormalized here for rapid querying and reporting without joining to the reference genome dimension. Critical for clinical interpretation — variant coordinates are build-specific.
reference: NCBI RefSeq; Genome Reference Consortium (GRC); ACMG Variant Interpretation Guidelines

description: Human-readable, externally referenceable business identifier for this alignment result (e.g., ALN-2024-00123456). Used in LIMS reports, bioinformatics dashboards, and regulatory submissions to uniquely identify an alignment output without exposing surrogate keys. Satisfies BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.

Sequencing instrument platform used to generate the raw reads (e.g., Illumina NovaSeq, PacBio Revio, Oxford Nanopore PromethION). Platform determines read characteristics (length, error profile), applicable alignment tools, and QC thresholds. Required for method validation documentation and regulatory submissions.
reference: FDA IVD Submission Guidelines; ISO 15189; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

description: Classification of the sequencing assay type for which this alignment was performed: Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS), Whole Exome Sequencing (WES), targeted panel, RNA-seq, amplicon, or metagenomics. Determines applicable QC thresholds, coverage requirements, and downstream analysis workflows. Satisfies CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category.
reference: ACMG/AMP Sequencing Guidelines; ISO 15189; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA IVD Submission Guidelines

description: Ratio of reads mapping to the forward strand versus the reverse strand (forward_reads / total_mapped_reads). Expected value is approximately 0.5 for unstranded libraries. Significant deviation indicates strand bias, which can introduce systematic variant calling errors, particularly for SNP and indel detection.
reference: Picard CollectAlignmentSummaryMetrics; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines

description: Total number of sequencing reads in the input FASTQ file(s) submitted for alignment. Reflects sequencing depth and library complexity. Used to assess whether sufficient input data was provided for the intended application (e.g., WGS, WES, targeted panel). Key QC input metric.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub QC Metrics; ACMG/AMP Sequencing QC Guidelines

description: The date and time when this alignment result record was last modified, such as when QC status was updated after manual review or when supplementary metrics were appended. Supports audit trail and data governance requirements. Satisfies RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.
reference: GxP ALCOA+ Principles; ISO 27001; SOX Section 404

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual pipeline execution record in the bioinformatics domain. Primary key for the pipeline_run data product.

description: Total CPU core-hours consumed by this pipeline run across all compute nodes. Primary metric for cloud/HPC cost attribution, capacity planning, and per-sample computational cost reporting.

reference: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; GxP 21 CFR Part 11 Audit Trail; ISO 13485 Section 4.2.4

reference: ServiceNow Incident Classification; ISO 13485 Section 8.3 Nonconforming Output; Genomics Biotech Bioinformatics SOP

reference: ServiceNow Incident Management; Genomics Biotech Bioinformatics Failure Triage SOP

description: Estimated monetary cost in US Dollars for the compute resources consumed by this pipeline run, derived from CPU core-hours, memory, and storage metrics against cloud/HPC pricing. Used for per-sample cost attribution, project budget tracking, and COGS reporting.
reference: AWS Cost Explorer; Genomics Biotech Finance Cost Attribution Policy; SOX Financial Reporting

description: Numeric exit code returned by the pipeline process upon termination. Exit code 0 indicates successful completion; non-zero codes indicate specific failure modes. Used for automated failure classification and triage routing.
reference: POSIX Exit Code Standard; Nextflow/Snakemake Pipeline Exit Code Convention

business_glossary_term: Input FASTQ (Fast All Quality) File Path
description: Cloud or HPC storage path to the input FASTQ file(s) consumed by this pipeline run. FASTQ is the raw sequencing data format produced by NGS instruments. Required for data lineage tracking, reprocessing, and audit trail from raw data to result.
reference: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; HIPAA 45 CFR 164.312 Data Integrity; ISO 27001 Information Asset Management

description: Average number of sequencing reads aligned to each base position in the target region or genome. A key QC metric indicating sequencing depth adequacy. Minimum thresholds vary by assay type (e.g., 30x for WGS, 100x for targeted panels).
reference: CAP NGS Checklist; FDA Guidance on NGS-Based IVD Tests; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; ISO 15189

business_glossary_term: Output BAM (Binary Alignment Map) File Path
description: Cloud or HPC storage path to the output BAM (Binary Alignment Map) file produced by alignment pipeline runs. BAM is the standard compressed binary format for aligned sequencing reads. Used for downstream variant calling and data lineage.
reference: SAM/BAM Format Specification (hts-specs); NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; HIPAA 45 CFR 164.312

description: Cloud or HPC storage path to the final analytical report or summary output artifact (e.g., QC report, annotation summary, CNV report) generated by this pipeline run. Used for result delivery to downstream consumers and regulatory documentation.
reference: Veeva Vault Document Management; ISO 13485 Section 4.2.4 Document Control; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

business_glossary_term: Output VCF (Variant Call Format) File Path
description: Cloud or HPC storage path to the output VCF (Variant Call Format) file produced by variant calling pipeline runs. VCF is the standard format for representing SNPs, indels, and structural variants. Central artifact for clinical and research genomic interpretation.
reference: VCF Format Specification v4.3 (hts-specs); FDA Guidance on NGS-Based IVD Tests; IVDR EU 2017/746

description: Maximum RAM (in gigabytes) consumed at any point during this pipeline run. Used for resource right-sizing, out-of-memory failure diagnosis, and HPC/cloud instance type optimization.
reference: AWS EC2 Instance Sizing Guidelines; HPC Resource Management Best Practices

business_glossary_term: Percentage of Bases Above Phred Score Q30
description: Percentage of sequencing bases with a Phred quality score of 30 or higher, indicating 99.9% base call accuracy. A primary sequencing QC metric used to assess run quality before downstream analysis. Industry standard threshold is ≥80%.
reference: Illumina Sequencing Quality Metrics; CAP NGS Checklist; FDA Guidance on NGS-Based IVD Tests; Phred Score Standard

description: Percentage of total sequencing reads that successfully aligned to the reference genome. A key alignment QC metric; low mapping rates indicate sample quality issues, contamination, or reference genome mismatch.
reference: SAMtools Alignment Statistics; CAP NGS Checklist; ISO 15189 Section 5.5

description: Classification of the bioinformatics pipeline category executed in this run. Drives downstream routing, result schema expectations, and domain-specific SLA thresholds. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: alignment|variant_calling|annotation|cnv_analysis|snp_genotyping|methylation|rna_seq|gene_editing_qc — promote to reference product]
reference: Genomics England Bioinformatics Pipeline Classification; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Human-readable description of the specific QC metric(s) that caused this pipeline run to fail QC assessment (e.g., 'Mean coverage depth 18x below 30x threshold', 'Mapping rate 62% below 80% threshold'). Populated only when qc_pass_flag is False.
reference: CAP NGS Checklist; ISO 13485 Section 8.3 Nonconforming Output; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Boolean indicator of whether this pipeline run passed all defined QC thresholds (coverage depth, mapping rate, Phred score, variant count sanity checks). Drives automated downstream routing — only QC-passed runs proceed to clinical or research reporting.
reference: CAP NGS Checklist; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; ISO 13485 Section 8.2.4; FDA Guidance on NGS-Based IVD Tests

description: Regulatory classification of the intended use of this pipeline run's outputs. IVD (In Vitro Diagnostic) runs are subject to FDA/IVDR validation requirements; RUO (Research Use Only) runs have different compliance obligations. Drives audit trail depth and result release controls.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 820 IVD Regulations; IVDR EU 2017/746; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; ISO 13485

description: Indicates whether this pipeline run is a reprocessing of a previously executed run (e.g., triggered by QC failure, pipeline version upgrade, or parameter correction). When True, data_lineage_run_id should reference the original run.
reference: GxP 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 13485 Section 8.3; CAP NGS Checklist

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier assigned to this pipeline execution at submission time. Used for cross-system traceability, SLA tracking, and audit references across LIMS, BaseSpace, and downstream reporting systems.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub Run Naming Convention; LabVantage LIMS Run Identifier Standard

description: Current lifecycle state of the pipeline execution. Drives operational dashboards, SLA breach alerting, failure triage workflows, and batch-level completion monitoring. Transitions: queued → running → completed | failed | cancelled.
reference: ServiceNow Workflow State Model; ISO 13485 Section 8.3 Nonconforming Output

description: The type of genomic sequencing assay whose data is being processed in this pipeline run (e.g., WGS — Whole Genome Sequencing, WES — Whole Exome Sequencing, targeted panel). Determines applicable pipeline parameters, QC thresholds, and regulatory classification.
reference: FDA Guidance on Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) Tests; IVDR EU 2017/746; CAP NGS Checklist

description: Indicates whether this pipeline run exceeded its defined SLA target TAT. Populated upon run completion. Drives SLA breach alerting, escalation workflows in ServiceNow, and operational performance reporting.
reference: ServiceNow SLA Management; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; Genomics Biotech SLA Policy

business_glossary_term: Service Level Agreement (SLA) Target Turnaround Time (Hours)
description: The contracted or internally defined SLA target for Turnaround Time (TAT) in hours for this pipeline run, based on assay type and regulatory classification. Used to assess SLA compliance by comparing against actual wall-clock duration.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 TAT Requirements; CAP Laboratory Accreditation; Genomics Biotech SLA Policy

description: The date and time when the pipeline run transitioned from queued to actively executing on the compute environment. Used to calculate queue wait time (start_timestamp minus submission_timestamp) and actual wall-clock execution duration.
reference: ISO 8601 Timestamp Standard; ServiceNow SLA Tracking

description: Total intermediate and output storage consumed by this pipeline run in gigabytes. Includes FASTQ inputs, BAM alignment files, VCF outputs, and annotation artifacts. Used for storage cost attribution and capacity planning.
reference: AWS S3 Storage Cost Model; Genomics Biotech Data Retention Policy; ISO 27001 Asset Management

description: The date and time when this pipeline run was submitted to the compute queue. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for SLA measurement start, TAT (Turnaround Time) calculation, and queue wait-time analytics.
reference: ISO 8601 Timestamp Standard; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 TAT Requirements

description: Total number of sequencing reads processed by this pipeline run. Used as a primary input volume metric for QC assessment, cost normalization, and performance benchmarking across pipeline runs.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub Run Metrics; CAP NGS Checklist; FDA Guidance on NGS-Based IVD Tests

description: Indicates whether test results for this specification must be included on the Certificate of Analysis (COA) provided to customers. True for customer-facing specifications, false for internal-only tests.

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this QC specification record. Tracks specification change history.

reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211.192 Out of Specification Results

description: Textual description of acceptance criteria for qualitative or pass/fail tests (e.g., 'No visible particulates', 'Amplification curve within 3 Ct of reference', 'Sterility test shows no growth').

reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 820 Quality System Regulation

description: Required sample size or sampling plan for the test (e.g., 'n=3 replicates', 'AQL 1.5', '10 units per lot'). Supports statistical quality control.
reference: ISO 2859 Sampling Procedures for Inspection by Attributes

description: Business identifier for the QC specification. Unique alphanumeric code used in quality documentation and Certificate of Analysis (COA) references.

reference: ICH Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria

description: Current lifecycle status of the QC specification: draft (in development), under_review (pending approval), approved (authorized for use), active (currently enforced), superseded (replaced by newer version), obsolete (no longer valid).

description: Version number of the QC specification following semantic versioning (e.g., 1.0, 2.1, 3.0.1). Supports change control and regulatory traceability.
Nominal or target value for the analytical parameter. Represents the ideal measurement outcome within the specification range.

Required frequency of testing for this specification: per_lot (every manufacturing lot), per_batch (every production batch), periodic (scheduled intervals), skip_lot (reduced testing per approved plan), continuous (in-process monitoring).
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 211 Good Manufacturing Practice

description: Name of the analytical test method used to evaluate the reagent (e.g., HPLC Purity Analysis, Endotoxin LAL Assay, qPCR Functional Performance).

Unit of measurement for the analytical parameter (e.g., mg/mL, EU/mL, %, U/mg, Ct value, copies/µL). Null for qualitative or pass/fail tests.
Maximum acceptable value for numeric acceptance criteria. Null if not applicable (e.g., pass/fail tests).

business_glossary_term: American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) Secondary Findings Flag
description: Indicates whether the gene is on the ACMG list of genes recommended for reporting of secondary findings in clinical sequencing. Critical for clinical laboratory compliance and incidental findings workflows.
Comma-separated list of disease phenotypes or clinical conditions associated with variants in this gene. Supports clinical assay design and variant prioritization workflows.

Chromosome on which the gene is located (1-22, X, Y, or MT for mitochondrial). Critical for cytogenetic reporting and structural variant analysis.

business_glossary_term: Loss-of-Function Observed/Expected Upper Bound Fraction (LOEUF) Constraint Metric
description: Loss-of-Function Observed/Expected Upper Bound Fraction from gnomAD, a continuous measure of gene constraint. Lower LOEUF scores indicate greater intolerance to loss-of-function variants.

business_glossary_term: Probability of Loss-of-Function Intolerance (pLI) Constraint Metric
description: Probability of Loss-of-Function Intolerance score from gnomAD, indicating the gene's tolerance to inactivating variants. High pLI (>0.9) suggests the gene is intolerant to loss-of-function variants.
Timestamp when this gene model record was first created in the reference data catalog. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking for regulatory compliance.
Free-text notes from the data curation team documenting special considerations, known issues, or manual overrides applied to this gene model. Supports knowledge transfer and audit trails.
Date on which this gene model version was superseded or retired. Null for currently active versions. Supports temporal queries and regulatory audit trails.
Date from which this gene model version became effective and available for use in production annotation pipelines and clinical assays.
Genomic coordinate of the gene end position (3' end) in base pairs, relative to the reference genome build. Defines the gene boundary for annotation pipelines.
Stable Ensembl gene identifier used for cross-referencing with Ensembl genome browser and annotation databases.
NCBI Entrez Gene ID, the primary identifier used in NCBI databases including Gene, PubMed, and ClinVar for gene-level cross-referencing.
Indicates whether the gene is essential for cell viability or organism survival based on functional genomics studies. Used in CRISPR screen analysis and drug target prioritization.
reference: DepMap (Cancer Dependency Map), OGEE (Online Gene Essentiality Database)

description: Functional classification of the gene based on its molecular product type. Determines the gene's role in cellular processes and influences analysis pipelines. Free-text description of the gene's known or predicted function, biological role, and clinical significance. Supports manual curation and knowledge base enrichment.
Gene family or superfamily to which this gene belongs (e.g., 'kinase', 'G-protein coupled receptor', 'immunoglobulin'). Supports functional enrichment analysis and pathway mapping.
Total length of the gene in base pairs from start to end position. Used for coverage depth normalization and sequencing quality metrics.
Full descriptive name of the gene, providing human-readable context for the gene symbol (e.g., 'tumor protein p53' for TP53).
Current curation status of the gene record in the reference catalog. Active genes are approved for use in production pipelines; retired or withdrawn genes require remapping.
Comma-separated list of alternative names and synonyms for the gene. Enhances search and cross-referencing capabilities across literature and databases.
Version identifier for this gene model record, tracking updates to gene coordinates, annotations, or metadata over time. Ensures reproducibility and audit trail for regulatory compliance.
Reference genome assembly version used for gene coordinates (e.g., GRCh38/hg38, GRCh37/hg19, T2T-CHM13). Essential for coordinate liftover and reproducible variant interpretation.
Quantitative score indicating the likelihood that loss of one gene copy (haploinsufficiency) causes disease. Used for copy number variant interpretation and dosage sensitivity analysis.

business_glossary_term: HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (HGNC) Gene Symbol
description: Official gene symbol assigned by HGNC, the authoritative naming body for human genes. This is the primary human-readable identifier for the gene.
Date when this gene model record was last reviewed and curated by the bioinformatics or clinical genomics team. Supports data quality monitoring and refresh scheduling.
High-level classification of the locus type as defined by HGNC. Groups genes by their primary molecular function category.
Detailed locus type classification providing finer granularity than locus group (e.g., 'gene with protein product', 'RNA, long non-coding').

business_glossary_term: Matched Annotation from NCBI and EMBL-EBI (MANE) Select Transcript Identifier (ID)
description: MANE Select transcript identifier representing the gold-standard transcript for clinical reporting, jointly curated by NCBI and Ensembl.

description: Timestamp when this gene model record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trails, and downstream data refresh orchestration.

business_glossary_term: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) Identifier (ID)
description: OMIM identifier linking the gene to known genetic disorders and phenotypes. Used for clinical variant interpretation and disease association reporting.
Indicates whether the gene has known pharmacogenomic associations affecting drug metabolism, efficacy, or toxicity. Used for precision medicine and clinical decision support.
reference: PharmGKB (Pharmacogenomics Knowledge Base), CPIC (Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium)

description: Comma-separated list of previous or alias gene symbols for this gene. Supports legacy data migration and cross-reference mapping.
Genomic coordinate of the gene start position (5' end) in base pairs, relative to the reference genome build. Used for variant mapping and gene overlap analysis.
DNA strand on which the gene is encoded: '+' for forward/sense strand, '-' for reverse/antisense strand. Critical for transcript orientation and variant effect prediction.
Number of known transcript isoforms for this gene. Indicates alternative splicing complexity and impacts variant annotation strategies.
Identifier of the canonical or representative transcript for this gene, used as the default for variant annotation and clinical reporting.
reference: Ensembl, MANE (Matched Annotation from NCBI and EMBL-EBI)

description: Quantitative score indicating the likelihood that gain of one gene copy (triplosensitivity) causes disease. Used for copy number variant interpretation and dosage sensitivity analysis.
Unique identifier for the reference genome assembly record. Primary key.
Foreign key reference to the genome_assembly_id of the newer assembly that supersedes this one. Null if this assembly is current or has not been superseded.
Version identifier of the gene annotation track associated with this assembly (e.g., GENCODE v42, Ensembl 109). Gene annotations are versioned independently of the assembly.
Official accession identifier assigned by the source authority (NCBI/INSDC format: GCA_ for GenBank, GCF_ for RefSeq). Serves as the globally unique external identifier for this assembly build.
reference: NCBI Assembly Database; INSDC (International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration)

description: Alternative or legacy name for the assembly (e.g., hg38 for GRCh38, mm10 for GRCm38). Used for cross-referencing with external tools and historical datasets.
reference: UCSC Genome Browser; Ensembl Genome Browser

description: Degree of completeness and contiguity of the assembly. Chromosome = fully assembled chromosomes; Scaffold = ordered contigs with gaps; Contig = unordered contiguous sequences; Complete Genome = fully closed, telomere-to-telomere.
reference: NCBI Assembly Database; Genome Reference Consortium (GRC)

description: Bioinformatics software and algorithm used to assemble the genome (e.g., FALCON, Canu, DISCOVAR, SPAdes). Important for reproducibility and quality assessment.
Human-readable name of the genome assembly (e.g., GRCh38, T2T-CHM13v2.0, GRCm39). This is the canonical label used across all bioinformatics pipelines and publications.

Lifecycle status of the assembly. Active = currently used in production pipelines; deprecated = no longer recommended but still accessible; superseded = replaced by a newer version; archived = retained for historical reproducibility only.

Ploidy and structural representation of the assembly. Haploid = single consensus sequence; diploid = phased maternal/paternal; haploid-with-alt-loci = primary assembly plus alternate haplotype scaffolds.
Path to the Bowtie2 index files for this assembly. Alternative aligner index used in some RNA-seq and ChIP-seq pipelines.
Path to the BWA (Burrows-Wheeler Aligner) index files for this assembly. Required for read alignment in NGS pipelines.
Total number of chromosomes represented in the assembly, including autosomes, sex chromosomes, and mitochondrial DNA where applicable.
reference: Genome Reference Consortium (GRC); NCBI Assembly Database

description: Total number of contiguous sequences (contigs) in the assembly. Lower contig count indicates higher assembly contiguity and quality.
reference: NCBI Assembly Database; Genome Reference Consortium (GRC)

description: N50 statistic for contigs: the length at which 50% of the total assembly length is contained in contigs of this size or larger. Key quality metric for assembly contiguity.
reference: Genome Assembly Quality Metrics; NCBI Assembly Database

description: Average sequencing coverage depth (fold coverage) used to generate the assembly. Higher coverage generally indicates higher assembly accuracy.
reference: NGS Quality Metrics; Genome Assembly Best Practices

description: Timestamp when this genome assembly record was first created in the Genomics Biotech reference data catalog. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
reference: ISO 8601 Timestamp Format; ISO 27001 Information Security

description: Path to the cytoband file defining chromosome banding patterns (Giemsa staining regions). Used for cytogenetic coordinate mapping and visualization.
Date on which this assembly was officially deprecated by the source authority or by Genomics Biotech internal policy. Null if the assembly is still active.
reference: Genome Reference Consortium (GRC) Lifecycle Policy; ISO 8601 Date Format

description: Cloud storage or file system path to the primary FASTA file containing the assembly sequences. This is the authoritative artifact used by all downstream pipelines.
reference: FASTA Format Specification; AWS S3; Azure Blob Storage; Google Cloud Storage

description: MD5 hash of the FASTA file for integrity verification. Ensures the file has not been corrupted or tampered with during transfer or storage.
reference: MD5 Message-Digest Algorithm (RFC 1321); ISO 27001 Information Security

description: Percentage of guanine (G) and cytosine (C) bases in the total assembly sequence. Species-specific characteristic used for quality control and comparative genomics.
Path to the GFF3 file containing genomic features and annotations. Alternative to GTF, used by some annotation pipelines and genome browsers.
Path to the GTF file containing gene annotations (exons, transcripts, genes) for this assembly. Used by RNA-seq and variant annotation pipelines.
Path to the FASTA index file (.fai) used by bioinformatics tools (e.g., samtools, GATK) for rapid random access to sequences.
reference: SAMtools FASTA Index Format; GATK Best Practices

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this is the primary/default assembly for the organism. True = primary assembly used by default in all pipelines; False = alternate or legacy assembly.
reference: Genome Reference Consortium (GRC); NCBI Assembly Database

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this assembly is recognized as a community reference standard (e.g., GRCh38 for human). True = reference standard; False = non-standard or custom assembly.
reference: Genome Reference Consortium (GRC); FDA Guidance on NGS-Based Oncology Panels

description: Free-text field for additional metadata, known issues, usage recommendations, or special handling instructions for this assembly (e.g., 'Contains unresolved centromeric gaps', 'Recommended for clinical variant calling').
Common or vernacular name of the organism (e.g., human, mouse, thale cress). Used for user-facing displays and non-technical reporting.
Scientific name of the organism for which this genome assembly was built (e.g., Homo sapiens, Mus musculus, Arabidopsis thaliana).
Incremental patch or update number applied to the base assembly (e.g., p13 for GRCh38.p13). Patches correct errors or add alternate loci without changing the primary coordinate system.
reference: Genome Reference Consortium (GRC) Patch Release Policy

description: Number of complete sets of chromosomes in the organism. Haploid = one set (e.g., bacteria, haploid yeast); diploid = two sets (e.g., human, mouse); polyploid = more than two sets (e.g., wheat, some plants).
Date on which this assembly version was officially released by the source authority. Critical for reproducibility and version control in genomic analyses.
Total number of scaffolds in the assembly. Scaffolds are ordered and oriented contigs connected by gaps of estimated size.
reference: NCBI Assembly Database; Genome Reference Consortium (GRC)

description: N50 statistic for scaffolds: the length at which 50% of the total assembly length is contained in scaffolds of this size or larger. Higher values indicate better long-range contiguity.
reference: Genome Assembly Quality Metrics; NCBI Assembly Database

description: Path to the sequence dictionary file (.dict) required by GATK and Picard tools. Contains metadata about each sequence (chromosome) in the assembly.
Primary sequencing platform(s) used to generate the assembly (e.g., Illumina HiSeq, PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore, Sanger). Relevant for understanding assembly characteristics and error profiles.

description: Organization or consortium responsible for generating and maintaining this assembly (e.g., GRC = Genome Reference Consortium, T2T = Telomere-to-Telomere Consortium).

description: Name of the organization or consortium that submitted the assembly to the public database (e.g., Genome Reference Consortium, Broad Institute, Sanger Institute).
NCBI Taxonomy database identifier for the organism. Enables linkage to external biological databases and phylogenetic classification.

Boolean flag indicating whether this transcript is designated as the canonical (representative) transcript for the gene. Genomic coordinate (1-based) of the transcript end position (transcription termination site). Used for genomic range queries and variant overlap detection.
Total length of the transcript in base pairs, including all exons from transcription start to transcription end. Used for transcript size filtering and coverage depth calculations in sequencing QC.
Human-readable name or symbol for the transcript, often derived from the gene symbol with a transcript-specific suffix (e.g., BRCA1-201, TP53-001).

Genomic coordinate (1-based) of the 5' UTR end position (immediately before CDS start). Null for non-coding transcripts or transcripts without annotated 5' UTR. Used for regulatory variant analysis.

Genomic coordinate (1-based) of the 5' UTR start position (transcript start before the CDS). Null for non-coding transcripts or transcripts without annotated 5' UTR. Used for regulatory variant analysis.

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code of the country from which the shipment originates (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Required for import/export regulatory compliance and customs documentation.
reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations, WCO

description: Identifier of the site, laboratory, or facility from which the specimens are dispatched. References the internal site/facility master. Used for inter-site chain-of-custody and import/export compliance.

Type of temperature-controlled packaging used for the shipment. 'dry_ice' = solid CO2 for frozen specimens; 'ln2_shipper' = liquid nitrogen dry shipper for ultra-low temperature; 'ambient' = room temperature; 'refrigerated' = 2–8°C cold pack; 'controlled_ambient' = validated ambient range packaging. Critical for specimen integrity and IATA compliance.
reference: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations P650, IATA Special Provision A140, ISO 15189:2022

description: Indicates whether all Protected Health Information (PHI) associated with the specimens in this shipment has been de-identified in accordance with HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods prior to transfer. True = de-identified; False = PHI present, full HIPAA safeguards apply.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514, GDPR Article 4, NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Assessment of the shipment condition recorded by the receiving laboratory upon physical receipt. 'acceptable' = specimens received in satisfactory condition; 'compromised' = packaging or specimen integrity concerns noted; 'rejected' = shipment rejected and returned; 'pending_review' = condition under investigation. Drives specimen disposition workflow in LabVantage LIMS.

Free-text notes recorded by the receiving laboratory at the time of receipt, documenting any observed discrepancies, packaging damage, specimen count mismatches, or temperature excursion details. Supports non-conformance investigation and regulatory reporting.
Name or employee identifier of the laboratory staff member who confirmed receipt of the shipment at the destination site. Required for chain-of-custody documentation and GxP audit trails.

Indicates whether the shipment is outbound (specimens leaving the originating site) or inbound (specimens arriving at the receiving site). Drives chain-of-custody workflow and import/export regulatory compliance checks.

Classifies the purpose of the shipment. 'clinical' = patient specimens for diagnostic or clinical trial use; 'research' = RUO specimens; 'qc' = Quality Control reference materials; 'biobank_transfer' = long-term storage transfer; 'cro_transfer' = transfer to/from a Contract Research Organization. Drives regulatory handling requirements and IRB consent validation.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 812, CLIA 42 CFR §493, ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Calendar date on which the shipment was physically dispatched by the originating site and collected by the carrier. BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category (date-level precision for manifest planning and SLA tracking).

Precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the shipment was handed over to the carrier. Provides exact chain-of-custody event time for regulatory audit trails and temperature excursion analysis.

Free-text field capturing any special handling, storage, or processing instructions for the carrier and receiving laboratory (e.g., 'Keep upright', 'Do not X-ray', 'Priority handling required'). Communicated on the physical manifest and shipping label.

Total number of individual specimens or aliquots included in this shipment manifest. Used for receipt reconciliation and chain-of-custody verification at the destination site. QUANTITATIVE_RESULT category.

Indicates whether a temperature excursion (deviation outside the validated acceptable range) was detected during transit. True = excursion detected; False = no excursion. Triggers specimen integrity review and potential quarantine workflow in LabVantage LIMS.

Maximum temperature recorded by the temperature monitoring device during transit, in degrees Celsius. Used to assess cold-chain integrity and determine whether specimens experienced a temperature excursion above the acceptable range.
reference: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations P650, ISO 15189:2022, FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Minimum temperature recorded by the temperature monitoring device during transit, in degrees Celsius. Used to assess cold-chain integrity and determine whether specimens experienced a temperature excursion below the acceptable range.
reference: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations P650, ISO 15189:2022, FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Unique identifier of the temperature monitoring device (e.g., data logger, indicator strip, or IoT sensor) placed inside the shipment packaging. Used to retrieve temperature excursion records and validate specimen integrity upon receipt.
reference: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations, ISO 15189:2022, FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Carrier-assigned tracking number or airway bill number for the shipment. Enables real-time shipment tracking and chain-of-custody verification with the logistics provider.

United Nations dangerous goods classification number applicable to the shipment contents (e.g., UN3373 for Biological Substance Category B, UN2814 for Infectious Substance Category A, UN1845 for dry ice). Required on shipping labels and documentation when dangerous_goods_flag = True.
reference: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations, UN Model Regulations, IATA UN 3373

description: Date and time at which the shipment manifest record was most recently modified. RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Supports GxP audit trail requirements, change tracking, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
Unique surrogate identifier for each storage state change or custody transfer event record in the chain-of-custody audit trail. Primary key of the storage_event product.

Reference to the specific aliquot (sub-divided portion of a specimen) involved in this storage event. Nullable when the event applies to the primary specimen rather than a derived aliquot. Populated from LabVantage LIMS aliquot tracking.

Reference to the storage location (freezer, rack, shelf, box, or position) to which the specimen or aliquot was moved or placed. Null for disposal or external transfer events where no internal destination exists.

Foreign key linking to quality.quality_deviation. Business justification: Storage events (temperature excursions, unauthorized access, location errors) trigger deviations. Labs document which storage event caused each deviation for regulatory compliance and audit trails.

Reference to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) protocol under which the specimen was collected and is being stored. Ensures that storage and custody actions are performed within the bounds of approved research protocols and informed consent agreements.
reference: IRB, HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164, GDPR Article 9, NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Reference to the LIMS-driven workflow task or work order that triggered or is associated with this storage event. Links the storage action to the broader laboratory workflow context (e.g., assay preparation, QC run, clinical testing batch).

Reference to the storage location (freezer, rack, shelf, box, or position) from which the specimen or aliquot was retrieved or transferred. Null for initial placement events where no prior location exists.

Reference to the laboratory operator or technician who physically performed the storage event (placement, retrieval, relocation, or transfer). Sourced from Oracle Cloud HCM workforce records and LabVantage LIMS user registry.
Reference to the primary biological specimen (parent sample) involved in this storage event. Links to the specimen master record in LabVantage LIMS for full sample metadata and IRB consent context.
reference: LabVantage LIMS, ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Reference to the user who provided the electronic acknowledgment or e-signature for this storage event. May differ from the operator who performed the physical action, supporting dual-control and supervisory sign-off workflows required under GxP.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11, GxP, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Date and time at which the electronic acknowledgment or e-signature was applied to this storage event record. Distinct from the event_timestamp (when the physical action occurred). Required for FDA 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail completeness.

Monotonically increasing integer representing the ordinal position of this storage event within the complete chain-of-custody history for the specimen or aliquot. Enables ordered reconstruction of the full custody timeline for forensic genomics, legal, and regulatory audit purposes.
reference: GxP, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, ISO 15189, CAP, forensic genomics standards

description: The barcode or 2D matrix code printed on the physical container (tube, vial, plate, cryovial) holding the specimen or aliquot at the time of this storage event. Scanned by the operator during the event to confirm physical identity and prevent sample mix-up errors.
reference: LabVantage LIMS, ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, GxP

description: Classification of the physical container holding the specimen or aliquot during this storage event. Determines applicable storage conditions, handling protocols, and compatible storage unit configurations.

Date and time at which this storage event record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Represents the record audit creation time, distinct from the event_timestamp which captures when the physical action occurred.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11, GxP, ISO 15189, ISO 27001

description: Indicates whether this storage event involved a deviation from the applicable SOP or standard storage protocol. True triggers a deviation investigation workflow in the quality management system (Veeva Vault or MasterControl) and requires documented justification.
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, FDA 21 CFR Part 211, ISO 13485, Veeva Vault

description: Indicates whether the storage event has received a valid electronic acknowledgment (e-signature) from the responsible operator or custodian in compliance with FDA 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements. True confirms the event is electronically signed and locked.

Human-readable, externally referenceable identifier for this storage event, formatted as SE-{YYYY}-{YYYYMMDD}-{sequence}. Used in audit reports, chain-of-custody documentation, and regulatory submissions to uniquely reference a specific custody transfer or placement event.

Current lifecycle state of the storage event record. Indicates whether the event has been completed, is pending electronic acknowledgment, was cancelled, encountered a failure condition, or is under supervisory review for compliance purposes.

The precise real-world date and time at which the storage state change or custody transfer physically occurred, recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. This is the principal business event time, distinct from the record audit timestamps. Critical for chain-of-custody sequencing and GxP compliance.
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, FDA 21 CFR Part 11

description: Categorical discriminator identifying the nature of the storage state change. Drives chain-of-custody logic and audit trail classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: initial_placement|relocation|retrieval|return|inter_section_transfer|external_transfer|disposal|quarantine_placement — promote to reference product]
reference: GxP, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, ISO 15189, CAP

description: Name of the external facility, partner laboratory, or clinical site to which the specimen or aliquot was transferred during an inter-site or external transfer event. Populated only for event_type = external_transfer. Supports chain-of-custody documentation for multi-site genomics studies.
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, HIPAA, GDPR

description: Shipping or courier tracking number associated with an external specimen transfer event. Enables end-to-end shipment traceability for specimens transferred to external sites, partner labs, or clinical collaborators. Populated only for event_type = external_transfer.
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, IATA P650 (Biological Substances), CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Cumulative number of freeze-thaw cycles the specimen or aliquot has undergone up to and including this storage event. Excessive freeze-thaw cycles degrade nucleic acid and protein integrity; this count is critical for sample quality assessment in genomic and clinical workflows.
reference: ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, GxP, CAP

description: Indicates whether this storage event record has been locked and made immutable following electronic acknowledgment and audit finalization. Immutable records cannot be modified or deleted, satisfying FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and GxP requirements for tamper-evident audit trails.

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Event Reference
description: The native event or transaction identifier assigned by LabVantage LIMS for this storage event. Enables bidirectional traceability between the Databricks Silver Layer data product and the operational LIMS system of record for reconciliation and audit purposes.

Indicates whether the specimen or aliquot involved in this storage event has been de-identified in accordance with HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods. True means PHI has been removed or anonymized; False means the specimen retains linkage to identifiable patient data.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164.514, GDPR Article 4, NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Indicates whether the specimen or aliquot was placed into or removed from quarantine status as part of this storage event. Quarantined samples are restricted from use in assays or downstream workflows pending investigation or quality review.
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Standardized reason for placing the specimen or aliquot into quarantine. Populated only when quarantine_flag is True. Drives investigation workflows and determines the path to quarantine release or disposal.
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Standardized reason code explaining the business justification for the storage event. Used for operational reporting, compliance audits, and workflow analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: routine_storage|retrieval_for_assay|transfer_to_external_site|quarantine|inter_section_transfer|disposal_scheduled|emergency_retrieval — promote to reference product]
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, CAP

description: Free-text narrative providing additional context or justification for the storage event beyond the standardized reason code. Captures operator notes, special circumstances, or deviations from standard operating procedures (SOPs) that require documentation.

The maximum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the specimen or aliquot type involved in this event, as defined by the applicable SOP or specimen handling protocol. Used in conjunction with required_temp_min_c to define the acceptable temperature window.

The minimum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the specimen or aliquot type involved in this event, as defined by the applicable SOP or specimen handling protocol. Used to evaluate whether a temperature excursion occurred.

Document identifier of the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) governing the storage event type performed. Links to the controlled document in MasterControl or Veeva Vault for audit trail completeness and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, FDA 21 CFR Part 211, MasterControl, Veeva Vault

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this storage event was originated or ingested into the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation between the lakehouse and upstream operational systems.
reference: GxP, ISO 27001, Snowflake Data Cloud, LabVantage LIMS

description: Volume of the specimen or aliquot in microliters (µL) at the time of this storage event. Captured to track volume consumption across retrieval events and to flag low-volume specimens that may be insufficient for planned assays.
reference: ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, LabVantage LIMS

description: Standardized code representing the required storage condition category for the specimen or aliquot at the destination location. Drives storage unit assignment logic and temperature monitoring alert thresholds in the LIMS and facility management systems.
reference: ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, GxP, LabVantage LIMS

description: Recorded ambient or storage unit temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of the storage event. Captured from connected monitoring systems or manually entered by the operator. Used to assess sample integrity and document temperature excursion conditions.
reference: GxP, ISO 15189, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Indicates whether a temperature excursion (deviation from the required storage temperature range) was detected or reported in association with this storage event. True signals a potential sample integrity risk requiring investigation and documentation per GxP and CLIA requirements.
reference: GxP, CLIA 42 CFR Part 493, ISO 15189, FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Date and time at which this storage event record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Tracks the last update for audit trail completeness and data lineage purposes. Immutable records will not have an updated_timestamp after locking.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11, GxP, ISO 15189, ISO 27001

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each temperature excursion event record in the Genomics Biotech cold-chain monitoring system. Primary key for this entity. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — a discrete GxP cold-chain compliance event with a clear lifecycle (detected, assessed, dispositioned, closed).

Foreign key linking to quality.quality_deviation. Business justification: Temperature excursions are a specific type of quality deviation requiring investigation and CAPA. Labs create deviation records for excursions to document impact assessment and corrective action.

business_glossary_term: Disposition Authorized By Employee Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Temperature excursion disposition decisions (use/quarantine/discard specimens) require documented approval by qualified personnel with appropriate training and authority. Critical for GxP compliance,

Reference to the specimen shipment manifest affected by the temperature excursion. Populated when the excursion occurs during transit rather than at a fixed storage location. Mutually exclusive with storage_location_id in most cases.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations; ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3

description: Reference to the physical storage location (freezer, refrigerator, cryogenic tank, cold room) where the excursion occurred. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE category (resource reference to the affected storage asset). Populated when the excursion is location-based rather than shipment-based.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3; LabVantage LIMS Storage Module

description: Predominant biological specimen type(s) affected by the excursion (e.g., whole blood, plasma, FFPE tissue, DNA extract, RNA extract, cell line). Informs the biological stability risk assessment since different specimen types have different thermal sensitivity profiles. Free text to accommodate diverse specimen types. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: whole_blood|plasma|serum|dna_extract|rna_extract|ffpe_tissue|cell_line|urine|csf — promote to reference product]
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 15189 Section 5.7; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Total number of individual biological specimens (samples, aliquots, tubes) present in the affected storage location or shipment at the time of the excursion. Used for impact scope assessment, risk quantification, and regulatory reporting. Populated during impact assessment phase.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.3; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Timestamp at which the automated alert notification was sent to responsible personnel (lab manager, QA, on-call staff) following excursion detection. Used to measure response time and assess SLA compliance for cold-chain incident response. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.2.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68

business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Reference Number
description: Reference number of the associated CAPA record in the quality management system (Veeva Vault or MasterControl) initiated as a result of this excursion. Enables cross-system traceability between the excursion event and the corrective action workflow.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100; Veeva Vault QMS

description: Indicates whether a formal Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) is required as a result of this temperature excursion. Driven by excursion severity category, recurrence pattern, and QA assessment. True triggers CAPA initiation in the quality management system (Veeva Vault or MasterControl).
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100; ICH Q10

description: Timestamp at which the temperature excursion record was formally closed in the quality management system, indicating all required actions (impact assessment, disposition, CAPA initiation if required) have been completed and reviewed. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Description of the immediate corrective action taken in response to the excursion (e.g., specimens transferred to backup freezer, equipment serviced, power restored, dry ice added). Distinct from the formal CAPA; captures the real-time remediation steps.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.5.1; SOP compliance

description: Timestamp when the temperature excursion record was first created in the system (LabVantage LIMS or integrated cold-chain monitoring platform). May differ from detection_timestamp if there is a lag in data entry. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 4.2.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

description: The real-world timestamp at which the temperature excursion was first detected by the monitoring device or alert system. This is the principal business event time for the excursion. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68; ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3

description: Reference number of the formal deviation report filed in the quality management system (Veeva Vault or MasterControl) documenting this temperature excursion. Required for GxP compliance, regulatory inspection readiness, and quality trending.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 211; Veeva Vault QMS

description: The formal disposition decision for the affected specimens following impact assessment. Use-as-is: specimens deemed unaffected; Conditional use: specimens usable with documented justification; Quarantine: specimens held pending further evaluation; Retest required: specimens require QC retesting before use; Discard: specimens deemed compromised and destroyed.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.3; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Scientific and regulatory justification for the disposition decision, including reference to stability data, specimen type thermal sensitivity, excursion magnitude, and duration. Required for GxP audit trail and regulatory submission support.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.3; ICH Q1A; FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Timestamp at which the formal disposition decision was made and recorded by the authorized reviewer. Establishes the timeline for regulatory audit purposes and tracks TAT (Turnaround Time) for excursion resolution. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Total duration of the temperature excursion in minutes, calculated from excursion_start_timestamp to excursion_end_timestamp. Stored as a business field to support threshold-based disposition rules and regulatory reporting without requiring runtime calculation. Null if excursion is ongoing.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISPE Good Distribution Practice Guide; ISO 13485 Section 7.5

description: Severity classification of the excursion based on magnitude and duration relative to defined thresholds. Drives escalation protocols, CAPA requirements, and regulatory notification obligations. Minor: within acceptable tolerance; Critical: significant risk to specimen integrity.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); FDA 21 CFR Part 211; ISO 13485 Section 8.3; ICH Q10

description: Timestamp at which the temperature returned within the acceptable range, marking the end of the excursion event. Null if the excursion is still ongoing. Used together with excursion_start_timestamp to determine total duration. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68; ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3

description: Human-readable, externally referenceable business identifier for the excursion event (e.g., EXC-2024-000123). Used in deviation reports, CAPA records, regulatory submissions, and customer communications. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); FDA 21 CFR Part 211; ISO 13485 Section 8.3

description: The source or mechanism by which the temperature excursion was detected. Automated monitor: continuous monitoring system alarm; Manual check: discovered during routine temperature log review; Shipment logger: data logger downloaded upon receipt; IoT sensor: real-time IoT platform alert; Third-party courier: reported by logistics provider.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 7.6; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: Timestamp at which the temperature first breached the defined alert threshold, marking the beginning of the excursion event. Used to calculate excursion duration and assess cumulative thermal exposure. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68; ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3

description: Current lifecycle state of the temperature excursion event workflow. Progresses from initial detection through impact assessment and disposition decision to closure. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: Classification of the excursion by the nature of the temperature deviation. High temperature indicates warming above upper threshold; low temperature indicates cooling below lower threshold; freeze-thaw indicates unintended freeze/thaw cycle; rapid change indicates rate-of-change violation; prolonged drift indicates slow sustained deviation.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISPE Good Distribution Practice Guide; ISO 13485 Section 7.5

description: Narrative summary of the impact assessment conducted to evaluate the effect of the temperature excursion on specimen integrity, assay validity, and downstream test results. Documents the scientific rationale used to support the disposition decision.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.3; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; ICH Q1A

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Excursion Reference
description: The source system reference identifier for this excursion record as assigned by LabVantage LIMS. Enables bidirectional traceability between the Databricks Silver Layer analytical record and the operational LIMS source of record for audit and reconciliation purposes.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); FDA 21 CFR Part 11; LabVantage LIMS

description: The lower temperature alert threshold configured on the monitoring device at the time of the excursion, expressed in degrees Celsius. Documents the threshold that was breached to trigger the excursion alert. Essential for audit trail and regulatory review.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 7.6; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: The highest temperature value recorded by the monitoring device during the excursion event, expressed in degrees Celsius. Critical for assessing heat degradation risk for biological specimens, nucleic acids, and reagents. Used in impact assessment and disposition decision logic. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER QUANTITATIVE_RESULT category.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3; IATA Perishable Cargo Regulations

description: The mean kinetic temperature (MKT) recorded during the excursion period, expressed in degrees Celsius. MKT is the single calculated temperature that, if maintained constantly, would produce the same thermal degradation as the actual variable temperature conditions experienced. Used in pharmaceutical and biological specimen stability assessments per ICH Q1A.
reference: ICH Q1A (Stability Testing); GxP (Good Practice Regulations); USP <1079>

description: The lowest temperature value recorded by the monitoring device during the excursion event, expressed in degrees Celsius. Critical for assessing freeze risk for biological specimens and reagents. Used in impact assessment and disposition decision logic.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3; IATA Perishable Cargo Regulations

description: Unique identifier of the temperature monitoring device (data logger, IoT sensor, continuous monitoring system) that recorded the excursion. Used for equipment traceability, calibration verification, and audit trail. Maps to the instrument/device asset register.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 7.6; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: The excursion_number of the most recent prior excursion at the same location or device, populated when recurrence_flag is True. Enables trend analysis and supports CAPA root cause investigation by linking related excursion events.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; ICH Q10

description: Indicates whether this excursion is a recurrence of a previously documented excursion at the same storage location or on the same monitoring device within a defined lookback period. Recurrent excursions trigger mandatory CAPA escalation and may indicate systemic equipment or process failure.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; ICH Q10 Section 3.2

description: Indicates whether this temperature excursion meets the criteria for mandatory regulatory reporting to a governing body (e.g., FDA, EMA, CAP, CLIA). Determined during impact assessment based on specimen type, intended use (IVD, clinical, GMP), and excursion severity.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 803; IVDR 2017/746; ISO 13485 Section 8.2.3; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Timestamp at which a responsible person acknowledged the excursion alert and initiated a response action (e.g., moved specimens, initiated repair, escalated). Used to calculate response time KPI and assess GxP compliance with cold-chain SOP requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.2.1; SOP compliance

description: Categorized root cause of the temperature excursion as determined during investigation. Used for trending, CAPA identification, and preventive action planning. Populated after investigation is complete. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equipment_failure|power_outage|door_left_open|improper_loading|calibration_drift|ambient_condition|transport_delay|human_error|unknown — promote to reference product]
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; ICH Q10 Section 3.2

description: Detailed narrative description of the identified root cause of the temperature excursion, as documented during the deviation investigation. Complements root_cause_category with specific contextual details for CAPA and regulatory review.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: The required storage temperature condition for the affected specimens or materials at the time of the excursion. Provides context for assessing the severity of the deviation relative to the required storage specification.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3; USP <1079>

description: Indicates which configured alert threshold was breached during the excursion: upper threshold (overheating), lower threshold (overcooling/freeze), or both (e.g., during a freeze-thaw cycle). Drives the type of impact assessment required.

Timestamp of the most recent modification to the temperature excursion record, including status changes, disposition updates, or impact assessment revisions. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 4.2.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

description: The upper temperature alert threshold configured on the monitoring device at the time of the excursion, expressed in degrees Celsius. Documents the threshold that was breached to trigger the excursion alert. Essential for audit trail and regulatory review.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 7.6; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: Percentage of total reads that successfully aligned to the reference genome. A key indicator of library quality and sample integrity. Typically expected to be >95% for high-quality human genomic libraries.
