description: Mean Phred quality score across all bases in the library. Phred scores represent the probability of a base call error (Q30 = 99.9% accuracy). Used to assess sequencing chemistry performance and overall run quality.

description: Average number of times each base in the target region (or genome for WGS) is sequenced, expressed in fold-coverage (X). Primary metric for assessing sequencing depth adequacy. Computed as total aligned bases divided by target region size.

description: Median number of times each base in the target region is sequenced, expressed in fold-coverage (X). Less sensitive to outlier regions than mean coverage; used alongside mean to assess coverage distribution skewness.

description: Assay-specific minimum mean coverage depth threshold (in X) that must be met for the library to pass QC. Defined in the assay specification and used to evaluate the qc_status determination. Varies by assay type (e.g., 30X for clinical WGS, 100X for somatic oncology panels).

description: The compression algorithm applied to the FASTQ file. Standard for NGS data is gzip (.gz). Determines decompression requirements for bioinformatics pipeline ingestion and storage cost calculations.
reference: FASTQ Format Specification; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — File Storage Standards

description: The informed consent status of the subject associated with this FASTQ file's sample. Governs permissible uses of the genomic data (research, clinical, secondary use). Withdrawn consent triggers data deletion or de-identification workflows per GDPR and HIPAA.
reference: GDPR Article 7 (Consent); HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR Part 164; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; ICH E6 GCP

description: The date and time when this FASTQ file record was first created in the sequencing data inventory (Silver Layer). Audit trail timestamp for data governance and lineage tracking.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — Audit Trails; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines; ISO 27001

description: The data sensitivity classification level assigned to this FASTQ file per Genomics Biotech data governance policy. Restricted = highest sensitivity (PHI/PII), Confidential = sensitive business data, Internal = general internal use, Public = no restrictions. Drives access control, encryption, and retention policies.
reference: ISO 27001 — Information Classification; HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR Part 164; GDPR Article 32; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Indicates whether this FASTQ file is encrypted at rest in cloud storage. Encryption is mandatory for PHI-containing files under HIPAA Security Rule and for GxP-regulated data. Supports security compliance auditing.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR Part 164.312; ISO 27001 — Cryptography Controls; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

description: The full file name of the FASTQ output file including extension (e.g., SampleA_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz). Follows Illumina naming conventions encoding sample, lane, read number, and index.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — FASTQ File Naming Convention; FASTQ Format Specification (Cock et al., 2010)

description: Cloud storage URI indicating the full path to the FASTQ file on BaseSpace or Amazon S3 (e.g., s3://genomics-biotech-seq/runs/RUN001/SampleA_R1.fastq.gz). Serves as the authoritative location reference for downstream bioinformatics pipeline access.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Storage API; AWS S3 Object Naming

description: The size of the FASTQ file in bytes as stored in cloud storage. Used for storage capacity planning, data transfer cost estimation, and file integrity verification. Compressed (gzip) size is recorded.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — File Metadata; AWS S3 Object Metadata

description: Current lifecycle status of the FASTQ file in the sequencing data inventory. Pending = demultiplexing in progress, Available = ready for pipeline consumption, Archived = moved to cold storage, Deleted = purged per retention policy, Failed = generation error, Quarantined = held for QC investigation.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — File Lifecycle Management; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines

description: The date and time when this FASTQ file was generated by the demultiplexing process. Represents the principal business event timestamp — the moment raw sequencing data became available as a FASTQ artifact. Used for TAT (Turnaround Time) calculations and data lineage.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — File Metadata; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines; CLIA TAT Requirements

description: The nucleotide index sequence (barcode) used to identify and demultiplex this sample from a multiplexed sequencing run. Composed of ACGT bases. Critical for validating correct sample assignment and detecting index hopping or cross-contamination.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Sample Sheet; Multiplexing and Demultiplexing Standards

description: Regulatory classification of the intended use of this sequencing data. RUO = Research Use Only, IVD = In Vitro Diagnostic (FDA-cleared/approved), LDT = Laboratory Developed Test (CLIA-regulated). Governs data handling, access controls, and regulatory reporting obligations.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 820; IVDR EU 2017/746; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA IVD Guidance

description: The MD5 cryptographic hash of the FASTQ file used to verify file integrity during transfer, storage, and archival. Mandatory for data integrity validation in GxP-regulated environments and regulatory submissions.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — Electronic Records; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines (MHRA, EMA); ISO 27001

business_glossary_term: Mean Phred Quality Score (Base Quality Score)
description: The mean Phred quality score (Q-score) across all bases in this FASTQ file. Phred scores represent the probability of a base call error (Q30 = 99.9% accuracy). A key QC metric for raw sequencing data quality assessment per NGS best practices.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — QC Metrics; Phred Quality Score Standard (Ewing & Green, 1998); ISO 15189

description: The mean length of sequencing reads in this FASTQ file measured in base pairs (bp). Reflects the sequencing chemistry and run configuration. Relevant for alignment pipeline parameter selection and quality benchmarking.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Parameters; FASTQ Format Specification

business_glossary_term: Percentage of Bases at Q30 or Above (Phred Score ≥30)
description: The percentage of bases in this FASTQ file with a Phred quality score of 30 or higher (≥Q30), indicating ≥99.9% base call accuracy. Industry-standard QC threshold for NGS data quality; typically ≥80% Q30 is required for clinical-grade sequencing.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — QC Metrics; FDA Guidance on NGS-Based IVD Devices; ISO 15189

description: The percentage of reads in this FASTQ file that passed the Illumina chastity filter (PF reads). Reads failing the filter are excluded from analysis. A key indicator of cluster quality and flow cell performance.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Demultiplexing Statistics; Illumina Cluster Density and PF Metrics

description: Indicates whether this FASTQ file is associated with Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined under HIPAA. When True, the file is subject to HIPAA Privacy and Security Rule requirements, access restrictions, and audit logging obligations. Drives data governance and access control enforcement.
reference: HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR Part 164; GDPR Article 9 (Special Category Data); NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Indicates whether this FASTQ file has passed all QC checks and is cleared for ingestion into bioinformatics analysis pipelines. When True, the file is eligible for alignment, variant calling, and downstream processing. Prevents failed or quarantined files from entering production pipelines.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Pipeline Trigger Logic; LabVantage LIMS — Workflow Automation

description: Free-text description of the reason for QC failure when qc_status is 'fail' or 'review'. Documents specific quality issues (e.g., low Q30 percentage, insufficient read count, adapter contamination) for root cause analysis and CAPA processes.
reference: ISO 15189; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP NGS Checklist; GxP CAPA Requirements

description: The QC assessment outcome for this FASTQ file based on Phred scores, read counts, and other quality metrics. Pass = meets all QC thresholds, Fail = below minimum thresholds, Review = borderline requiring manual review, Not Assessed = QC not yet performed. Governs eligibility for downstream bioinformatics processing.
reference: ISO 15189 — Medical Laboratories Quality; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP NGS Checklist; FDA NGS IVD Guidance

description: Designates the read type of this FASTQ file within a paired-end or indexed sequencing run. R1 = forward read, R2 = reverse read, I1 = index 1 (i7), I2 = index 2 (i5). Critical for demultiplexing validation and downstream alignment pipeline configuration.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — FASTQ File Naming Convention; NGS Library Preparation Standards

description: The calculated date on which this FASTQ file becomes eligible for deletion or archival based on the applied retention policy. Enables automated data lifecycle management and compliance with regulatory retention mandates.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493.1105; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164.530; GDPR Article 5(1)(e)

description: The data retention policy applied to this FASTQ file, governing how long the file must be retained before eligible for deletion or archival. Clinical data typically requires 10-year retention per CLIA/CAP; RUO data may follow shorter policies. Drives automated lifecycle management.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493.1105; CAP Accreditation Standards; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164.530; GDPR Article 5(1)(e); FDA 21 CFR Part 11

description: The type of NGS sequencing assay that produced this FASTQ file. Determines applicable bioinformatics pipelines, QC thresholds, and regulatory classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WGS|WES|targeted_panel|amplicon|RNA-seq|metagenomics|single_cell — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA Guidance on NGS-Based IVD Devices (2018); Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Application Types

description: The cloud storage tier in which this FASTQ file currently resides. Hot = frequently accessed (active analysis), Warm = infrequent access, Cold = rare access, Archive = long-term retention (e.g., AWS Glacier). Drives storage cost management and retrieval SLA expectations.
reference: AWS S3 Storage Classes; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Storage Management

description: The total number of sequencing reads contained in this FASTQ file after demultiplexing. A primary indicator of sequencing yield for this sample-lane combination. Used to assess whether minimum coverage depth thresholds are met for downstream analysis.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Demultiplexing Statistics; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: The date and time when this FASTQ file record was most recently modified in the sequencing data inventory. Tracks status changes, QC updates, and metadata corrections for audit compliance.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — Audit Trails; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines; ISO 27001

description: The date and time when this FASTQ file was successfully uploaded to cloud storage (BaseSpace or S3). Distinct from generation_timestamp; captures the transfer completion event for data availability tracking and SLA monitoring.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Upload API; AWS S3 Object Metadata

description: Unique surrogate identifier for this quality evaluation execution record. Primary key for the association.

business_glossary_term: File Quality Evaluation - Fastq File Id
description: Foreign key linking to the FASTQ file being evaluated in this quality check execution

business_glossary_term: File Quality Evaluation - Quality Rule Id
description: Foreign key linking to the quality rule definition applied in this evaluation
Identifier of the system, service, or user that executed this quality evaluation. Typically an automated pipeline service account, but may be a bioinformatician for manual QC review.
The time in seconds required to execute this quality rule against this FASTQ file. Used for pipeline performance monitoring and optimization.
Free-text description of why this rule failed or produced a warning for this file. Populated when rule_result is FAIL or WARNING. Supports troubleshooting and remediation.

The actual measured metric value from this FASTQ file that was compared against the rule threshold. For example, if rule checks minimum read count, this is the actual read count observed. Unit and interpretation depend on the rule type.
Boolean indicator of whether this file passed this specific quality rule. True = passed, False = failed. Simplified binary version of rule_result for filtering and aggregation.
The version identifier of the bioinformatics QC pipeline that executed this rule evaluation. Enables tracking of rule results across pipeline version changes and supports reproducibility.
Description of any automated or manual remediation action taken in response to this rule failure. Examples: file re-sequenced, sample flagged for review, data excluded from analysis.
The date and time when this quality rule was executed against this FASTQ file. Tracks when the evaluation occurred in the pipeline workflow.

The outcome of this quality rule evaluation. PASS = rule criteria met, FAIL = rule criteria not met, WARNING = borderline result, ERROR = execution error, SKIPPED = rule not applicable to this file type.

business_glossary_term: College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accredited Flag
description: Indicates whether this protocol is covered under a CAP-accredited laboratory's scope of accreditation. True = included in CAP accreditation scope; False = not within CAP scope. Relevant for clinical genomics laboratories reporting patient results.

business_glossary_term: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Validated Flag
description: Indicates whether this protocol has been validated under CLIA requirements for clinical laboratory use. True = CLIA validation completed and documented; False = not CLIA validated (RUO or research only). Required for protocols used in LDT or clinical reporting contexts.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP (College of American Pathologists) Accreditation Standards; ISO 15189

description: Comma-separated list of sequencing instrument models validated for use with this protocol (e.g., 'NovaSeq 6000, NovaSeq X Plus, NextSeq 2000'). Ensures run parameters are only applied to compatible hardware. Validated against instrument qualification records in LabVantage LIMS.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Instrument Compatibility; ISO 13485 Section 6.3; LabVantage LIMS

description: Timestamp when this sequencing protocol record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category. Populated automatically on insert and immutable thereafter. Supports GxP audit trail requirements.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); FDA 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); ISO 13485 Section 4.2.4; GDPR Article 5

description: Approved software tool used to demultiplex raw BCL files into per-sample FASTQ files for this protocol. Governs the bioinformatics pipeline entry point. BCL Convert is the current Illumina-recommended tool; DRAGEN provides accelerated on-instrument demultiplexing.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Demultiplexing Configuration; NGS Best Practices

description: Date on which this protocol version became (or becomes) effective for use in sequencing operations. Serves as the EFFECTIVE_FROM category. Protocols may not be used in regulated runs before this date. Managed through GxP change control in MasterControl.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 4.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 820; MasterControl

description: Specific flow cell cartridge type required by this protocol (e.g., 'S4 Flow Cell', 'SP Flow Cell', 'P2 Flow Cell', '25B Flow Cell'). Determines lane count, cluster capacity, and maximum data output. Must match the instrument model and run configuration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: S1|S2|S4|SP|P1|P2|P3|25B|nano — promote to reference product]
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Flow Cell Configuration; NGS Best Practices

description: Regulatory practice classification applicable to runs executed under this protocol. GMP = Good Manufacturing Practice (production reagents); GLP = Good Laboratory Practice (non-clinical studies); GCP = Good Clinical Practice (clinical trials); non-GxP = research use. Determines documentation, validation, and audit requirements.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); FDA 21 CFR Parts 210/211 (GMP); ICH E6 (GCP); OECD GLP Principles

description: Number of cycles for the Index 1 (i7) read used in multiplexing to demultiplex samples on a shared flow cell. Typically 8 or 10 cycles. Required for all multiplexed library pools. Null for non-indexed single-sample runs.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Multiplexing Configuration; NGS Demultiplexing Standards

description: Number of cycles for the Index 2 (i5) read used in dual-index multiplexing schemes. Typically 8 or 10 cycles. Null for single-index or non-indexed protocols. Dual indexing reduces index-hopping artifacts in high-multiplex runs.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Multiplexing Configuration; NGS Demultiplexing Standards

description: Regulatory classification of the protocol's intended use. RUO = Research Use Only; IVD = In Vitro Diagnostic (FDA-cleared); LDT = Laboratory Developed Test (CLIA-regulated); CE-IVD = EU Conformité Européenne In Vitro Diagnostic. Determines applicable regulatory framework, labeling requirements, and permissible clinical use.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 820 (IVD); IVDR EU 2017/746 (CE-IVD); CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 (LDT); ISO 13485

description: Maximum acceptable cluster density on the flow cell surface in K/mm². Exceeding this threshold causes cluster overlap (over-clustering), degrading base call quality and Q30 scores. Paired with min_cluster_density to define the acceptable loading range.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Flow Cell QC; NGS Best Practices

description: Maximum acceptable DNA insert size in base pairs for library fragments. Inserts exceeding this threshold may indicate insufficient fragmentation, leading to reduced cluster density and read-through artifacts. Paired with min_insert_size_bp to define the acceptable library size range.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Library QC; NGS Library Preparation Best Practices; ISO 15189 Section 5.5

description: Minimum acceptable cluster density on the flow cell surface, expressed in thousands of clusters per square millimeter (K/mm²). Below this threshold, insufficient data yield is expected. Used as a pre-run and mid-run QC gate in Illumina BaseSpace.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Flow Cell QC; NGS Best Practices

description: Minimum acceptable DNA insert size in base pairs for library fragments sequenced under this protocol. Insert sizes below this threshold indicate over-fragmentation and may degrade paired-end alignment quality. Used as a library QC acceptance criterion in LabVantage LIMS.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Library QC; NGS Library Preparation Best Practices; ISO 15189 Section 5.5

description: Minimum acceptable percentage of bases with a Phred quality score of 30 or higher (Q30), indicating ≥99.9% base call accuracy. Industry-standard QC gate for sequencing run acceptance. Runs falling below this threshold are flagged for investigation or resequencing. Typically ≥75% for most NGS applications.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — QC Metrics; Phred Score Standard; ISO 15189 Section 5.5

description: Minimum acceptable total sequencing data yield in gigabases (Gb) per run or per sample lane, as required to achieve the target coverage depth. Runs not meeting this threshold trigger a QC failure and potential resequencing. Derived from target coverage, genome size, and read length.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run QC; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Number of allowable base mismatches in the index sequence during demultiplexing before a read is assigned to the 'undetermined' bin. Typically 0 or 1. Higher values increase sample assignment rates but risk index cross-contamination in high-multiplex pools.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Demultiplexing Parameters; NGS Best Practices

description: Maximum number of samples that can be pooled and multiplexed on a single flow cell lane under this protocol while maintaining the target coverage depth per sample. Governs library pooling decisions in LabVantage LIMS and run planning in BaseSpace.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Multiplexing Guidelines; NGS (Next-Generation Sequencing) Best Practices

description: Name or employee identifier of the scientist or team lead responsible for maintaining and updating this sequencing protocol. The protocol owner initiates change control requests and is accountable for scientific validity. Sourced from Oracle Cloud HCM.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 5.5; GxP (Good Practice Regulations); Oracle Cloud HCM

business_glossary_term: Protected Health Information (PHI) Data Generated Flag
description: Indicates whether sequencing runs executed under this protocol generate Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined by HIPAA. True = PHI is generated (clinical patient samples); False = no PHI (research/RUO samples). Governs data handling, storage, and access control requirements for resulting FASTQ and downstream files.
reference: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) 45 CFR Parts 160/164; GDPR Article 9 (Special Category Data); NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique code identifying this protocol and version (e.g., WGS-PCR-v2.1). Used as the business identifier across LIMS, BaseSpace, and regulatory submissions. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for MASTER_RESOURCE role.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Protocol Configuration; ISO 13485 Section 4.2

description: Full descriptive name of the sequencing protocol (e.g., 'Whole Genome Sequencing PCR-Free 150bp Paired-End'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used in reporting, SOP references, and customer-facing documentation.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Protocol Configuration; MasterControl Document Control

description: Number of sequencing cycles for Read 1 (R1), determining the read length in base pairs for the forward read. Common values include 75, 100, 150, 250 cycles. Directly impacts data quality, coverage, and FASTQ file size. Serves as the MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Parameters; NGS (Next-Generation Sequencing) Best Practices

description: Number of sequencing cycles for Read 2 (R2) in paired-end configurations. Null for single-end protocols. Must match R1 cycle count for symmetric paired-end runs or may differ for asymmetric configurations. Governs reverse read length in base pairs.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Parameters; NGS Best Practices

description: Specifies whether the sequencing run is configured for single-end or paired-end reads. Paired-end reads generate two reads per fragment (R1 and R2), improving alignment accuracy and variant calling. Directly governs flow cell programming and FASTQ output structure.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Configuration; NGS Best Practices

description: Standard reference genome assembly version used for alignment and variant calling under this protocol (e.g., GRCh38 for human, GRCm39 for mouse). Ensures reproducibility and comparability of genomic results across runs and cohorts. Aligns with NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy requirements.
reference: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; NCBI Reference Sequence Database; ACMG Variant Interpretation Standards

description: Date on which this protocol version was retired or superseded and is no longer approved for new sequencing runs. Serves as the EFFECTIVE_UNTIL category. Null for currently active protocols. Historical runs executed under this protocol remain valid after retirement.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 4.2; MasterControl Document Control

description: Classification of the genomic sequencing application this protocol supports. Serves as the CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Drives downstream bioinformatics pipeline selection and QC thresholds. WGS = Whole Genome Sequencing; WES = Whole Exome Sequencing; RNA-seq = RNA Sequencing.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Configuration; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Free-text narrative description of the sequencing protocol, including its scientific rationale, key distinguishing parameters, intended sample types, and any special handling requirements. Authored by the protocol owner and reviewed during the GxP approval process.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 4.2; MasterControl Document Control; Benchling R&D Notebook

description: Version of the SOP document referenced by sop_document_id that is current and approved for use with this protocol version. Ensures the protocol record is always linked to the correct procedural revision, supporting GxP change control.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 4.2.3; MasterControl Document Control

description: Specifies the strand orientation of the sequencing library for RNA-seq and methylation protocols. Unstranded = no strand information preserved; Forward = sense strand; Reverse = antisense strand. Critical for accurate transcript quantification and differential expression analysis. Null for DNA-based protocols.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — RNA-seq Configuration; ENCODE RNA-seq Standards

description: Protocol code of the newer version that replaces this protocol upon retirement. Null for the current active version. Enables forward navigation in the protocol version chain for change control traceability and migration of active runs.
reference: GxP (Good Practice Regulations); ISO 13485 Section 4.2.3; MasterControl Document Control

description: Recommended mean sequencing coverage depth (in X, e.g., 30X for WGS, 100X for WES) required to meet analytical sensitivity thresholds for this protocol. Used to calculate required cluster density and flow cell loading. Governs pass/fail criteria for sequencing run QC.
reference: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; ACMG Sequencing Standards; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

description: File path or artifact identifier for the BED (Browser Extensible Data) file defining the genomic target regions for targeted panel or WES protocols. Null for WGS protocols. reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Panel Configuration; UCSC Genome Browser BED Format Standard; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

business_glossary_term: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub Index Set ID

description: Indicates whether the index set provides adequate color (fluorescence channel) balance across all sequencing cycles on two-channel or four-channel chemistry instruments. 'balanced' = no spike-in required; 'unbalanced' = color imbalance detected; 'requires_spike_in' = PhiX or other spike-in control is mandatory. Prevents base-calling failures on patterned flow cells.

description: Comma-separated list of sequencing instrument models validated for use with this index set (e.g., 'NovaSeq 6000, NextSeq 550, MiSeq'). Ensures that run configuration and read cycle parameters are compatible with the index chemistry.

description: Comma-separated list of library preparation kit names or catalogue numbers validated for use with this index set (e.g., 'TruSeq DNA PCR-Free, TruSeq Stranded mRNA, Nextera DNA Flex'). Managed by sequencing operations to prevent incompatible kit-index pairings during run setup.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Library Prep Compatibility Matrix; LabVantage LIMS — Reagent Compatibility

description: Timestamp when this index set record was first created in the Genomics Biotech lakehouse data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and GxP record integrity requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

description: Date on which the index set was deprecated or retired from active use. Null if still active. Used to enforce that no new sequencing runs are configured with deprecated index sets and to support historical traceability.

description: Indicates whether the index set was manufactured under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) conditions as required for IVD or clinical use. True = GMP-manufactured; False = non-GMP (RUO grade). Drives quality management and supplier qualification requirements.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 820 — Quality System Regulation; ISO 13485 Section 7.5; GxP Guidelines

description: Nucleotide sequence of the i5 (read 2 side) index used in dual-index configurations. Null or empty for single-index sets. Stored as a representative or consensus sequence; individual per-sample i5 sequences are tracked at the library level.

description: Nucleotide sequence of the i7 (read 1 side) index used for sample identification during demultiplexing. Stored as a representative or consensus sequence for the set; individual per-sample i7 sequences are tracked at the library level. Validated against IUPAC nucleotide codes.

description: Total number of unique index sequences (barcodes) available in the set. Determines the maximum multiplexing capacity — i.e., the maximum number of samples that can be pooled in a single sequencing run using this index set.

description: Length of the index sequence in base pairs (bp), typically 6, 8, 10, or 12 bp. Determines the read cycle configuration on the sequencer and affects the number of unique indices available in the set. Must match the sequencing run setup parameters.

description: Classification of the indexing strategy used in the set. 'single' = single-end index (i7 only); 'dual' = dual-index (i7 + i5, may be combinatorial); 'UDI' = Unique Dual Index (each sample has a unique i7+i5 pair, preventing index hopping); 'combinatorial' = combinatorial dual index (i7 and i5 drawn from independent pools). Critical for demultiplexing configuration and index-hopping risk assessment.
reference: Illumina Technical Note — Indexed Sequencing Overview; SEQC2 Consortium Guidelines

description: Regulatory intended use classification for the index set. 'RUO' = Research Use Only; 'IVD' = In Vitro Diagnostic; 'LDT' = Laboratory Developed Test; 'research' = internal research; 'clinical' = clinical genomics applications; 'agricultural' = agricultural genomics; 'both' = dual RUO and clinical use. Governs which workflows and regulatory submissions this index set may support. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: RUO|IVD|LDT|research|clinical|agricultural|both — promote to reference product]
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 820 — Quality System Regulation; IVDR EU 2017/746; ISO 13485 Section 7.3

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Index Set ID

description: Maximum number of samples that can be pooled (multiplexed) in a single sequencing run using this index set while maintaining the minimum Hamming distance threshold. Derived from the validated index set design; used in pool design planning and run capacity management.

description: The minimum Hamming distance between any two index sequences within the set. A higher value (typically ≥3) reduces the risk of index misassignment during demultiplexing. Critical quality parameter for pool design validation and collision prevention.
reference: Illumina Technical Note — Index Collision and Hamming Distance; SEQC2 Consortium Guidelines

description: Free-text field for sequencing operations scientists to record additional context, known limitations, special handling instructions, or validation observations for this index set that are not captured in structured fields.

description: Recommended percentage of PhiX control library to spike into the pool when using this index set, to correct for color imbalance or low-diversity libraries. Expressed as a percentage of total library pool volume (e.g., 1.00, 5.00, 20.00). Zero if no spike-in is required.
reference: Illumina Technical Note — PhiX Control Library; Illumina Sequencing System Guide

description: Specifies the orientation in which the i5 index is read on the sequencer. description: FDA 510(k) clearance number, CE-IVD certificate number, or equivalent regulatory authorization number if the index set is part of a cleared or approved IVD product. Null for RUO-only index sets. Required for regulatory submissions and audit trails.

description: The sequencing chemistry type for which this index set is designed. Determines color balance requirements and base-calling algorithm compatibility. Current quality control disposition of the library. Determines whether the library is eligible for sequencing run loading. LIFECYCLE_STATUS (MASTER_RESOURCE category). Analytical method used to measure library concentration and/or size distribution. Affects confidence in concentration accuracy and downstream loading calculations. Indicates whether this library was prepared as a resequencing attempt for a previously failed or insufficient-coverage library (True = resequencing; False = original preparation). Supports TAT tracking, cost analysis, and failure rate reporting.

Required or actual storage temperature for the library in degrees Celsius (e.g., -20°C for long-term, 4°C for short-term). Supports cold chain compliance, stability monitoring, and deviation investigation.

Indicates whether the library preserves strand-of-origin information for RNA-seq or other strand-aware assays. description: Indicates whether a temperature excursion or cold chain breach was detected during shipping or storage of this flow cell (True = breach detected). Triggers quarantine workflow and quality investigation in LabVantage LIMS and Veeva Vault. A breached flow cell must not be used until cleared by QA.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.5.11 — Preservation of Product; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.142; GDP Guidelines

description: Date and time when the sequencing run was completed and the flow cell was fully consumed or removed from the instrument. Marks the end of the flow cell's active lifecycle. Used for TAT reporting, instrument utilization metrics, and inventory depletion tracking.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Completion Metadata; LabVantage LIMS

description: Timestamp when the flow cell master record was first created in the Genomics Biotech lakehouse, typically at the point of goods receipt registration. Supports audit trail requirements under GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, and SOX internal controls.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — Electronic Records; SOX Section 404; ISO 27001 — Audit Logging

description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the unit_cost field (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Enables multi-currency financial reporting and cost normalization across global procurement activities.

description: Date on which the consumed, failed, or expired flow cell was disposed of per the applicable disposal method. Required for environmental compliance records and GMP documentation of consumable lifecycle closure.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 261; ISO 13485 Section 4.2 — Record Control; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.67

description: Method used for disposal of the consumed or failed flow cell. Governs environmental health and safety (EHS) compliance for waste management. Options include standard laboratory waste, biohazardous waste, chemical waste, or return to supplier for failed/defective units.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 261 — Hazardous Waste; ISO 14001 — Environmental Management; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.67

description: Manufacturer-specified expiration date after which the flow cell must not be used for sequencing. Critical for GMP compliance, inventory management, and preventing use of expired consumables that could compromise sequencing quality. Monitored in SAP S/4HANA QM and LabVantage LIMS for automated expiry alerts.
reference: GMP 21 CFR Part 211.122; ISO 13485 Section 7.5.11 — Preservation of Product; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.150

description: Identifier of the Genomics Biotech facility (laboratory or sequencing center) where this flow cell is stored and used. Supports multi-site inventory management, site-level capacity planning, and regulatory site-specific compliance reporting.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 6.3 — Infrastructure; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 — Laboratory Requirements

description: Current lifecycle status of the physical flow cell consumable. Tracks the operational state from receipt through consumption or disposal. 'in_stock' = received and available; 'reserved' = allocated to a planned run; 'loaded' = currently on instrument; 'consumed' = run completed; 'failed' = quality failure; 'expired' = past expiry date; 'quarantined' = held for investigation. reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.5 — Production and Service Provision; LabVantage LIMS Inventory Status Workflow

description: Instrument-specific flow cell format designation indicating throughput tier and lane configuration (e.g., S1, S2, S4, SP for NovaSeq 6000; MID, HIGH for NextSeq 550; P1, P2, P3 for NovaSeq X). Determines maximum output (Gb), number of lanes, and cluster density specifications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: S1|S2|S4|SP|MID|HIGH|P1|P2|P3 — promote to reference product]
reference: Illumina Flow Cell Specification Sheets; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub Metadata Standards

description: The sequencing instrument platform for which this flow cell is designed and compatible (e.g., NovaSeq 6000, NovaSeq X, NextSeq 2000, MiSeq). Governs compatibility rules for loading, reagent kits, and run parameters. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NovaSeq 6000|NovaSeq X|NextSeq 550|NextSeq 2000|MiSeq|HiSeq 4000|iSeq 100 — promote to reference product]
reference: Illumina Instrument Compatibility Matrix; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

Drives run parameter configuration and quality acceptance criteria. Also distinguishes Research Use Only (RUO) from In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD) use contexts for regulatory compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WGS|WES|targeted_sequencing|amplicon|RNA_seq|single_cell|RUO|IVD — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: FDA IVD Regulation 21 CFR Part 809; IVDR EU 2017/746; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

description: Indicates whether the flow cell is designed for single use only (True) or supports multiple sequencing runs (False). Governs reuse policies, disposal procedures, and run scheduling logic. Most modern Illumina flow cells are single-use; this flag supports future platform compatibility.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.5.11; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.70 — Production and Process Controls

description: Number of independent sequencing lanes on the flow cell (e.g., 1, 2, or 4 lanes for NovaSeq S1/S2/S4). Each lane can be loaded with a separate library pool, enabling multiplexing strategies. Drives capacity planning for sample batching and run scheduling.
reference: Illumina Flow Cell Specification Sheets; NGS Run Planning Best Practices

description: Barcode label scanned into LabVantage LIMS at receipt to register the flow cell in the laboratory inventory system. Used for physical tracking, chain-of-custody documentation, and automated workflow triggering in the LIMS. May differ from the manufacturer serial number.
reference: LabVantage LIMS — Inventory Management; ISO 15189 Section 5.4 — Pre-examination Processes

description: Date and time when the flow cell was physically loaded onto the sequencing instrument, marking the transition from 'reserved' to 'loaded' status. Recorded in Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub and LabVantage LIMS. Used for run scheduling, instrument utilization analysis, and TAT (Turnaround Time) calculations.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Metadata; LabVantage LIMS Workflow Tracking

description: Date the flow cell was manufactured by the supplier, as printed on the product label or Certificate of Analysis (COA). Used for shelf-life calculations, lot traceability, and quality investigations. Sourced from the COA accompanying the shipment.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.5.8 — Identification and Traceability; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: Manufacturer-specified maximum sequencing output in gigabases (Gb) achievable under optimal conditions for this flow cell type. Used for capacity planning, run design, and cost-per-sample calculations. Represents the principal quantitative performance specification of the flow cell resource.
reference: Illumina Flow Cell Specification Sheets; NGS Run Design Guidelines

description: Free-text field for laboratory personnel to record observations, anomalies, deviations, or special handling instructions associated with this flow cell. Examples include cold chain deviation details, physical damage observations, or QA hold reasons. Captured in LabVantage LIMS.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 4.2 — Document Control; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: SAP S/4HANA purchase order number under which this flow cell was procured. Provides procurement lineage linking the physical consumable to the financial transaction, supplier contract, and goods receipt documentation. Supports COGS tracking and financial reconciliation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Purchase Order Management; SOX Section 404 — Internal Controls

description: Date on which the incoming QC inspection was performed for this flow cell. Used for compliance audit trails, SOP adherence tracking, and calculating time-from-receipt-to-clearance metrics.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.4.3; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.84; SAP S/4HANA QM

description: Result of the incoming quality control inspection performed upon receipt of the flow cell. 'pending' = inspection not yet completed; 'passed' = meets acceptance criteria; 'failed' = does not meet criteria, quarantined; 'waived' = inspection waived per approved SOP (e.g., for pre-qualified lots). Managed in SAP S/4HANA QM and LabVantage LIMS.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.4.3 — Verification of Purchased Product; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.84; SAP S/4HANA QM

description: Maximum supported read length in base pairs (bp) for this flow cell type as specified by the manufacturer (e.g., 150 bp, 250 bp, 300 bp). Determines compatibility with library preparation protocols for WGS, WES, or targeted sequencing applications.
reference: Illumina Flow Cell Specification Sheets; NGS Library Preparation Guidelines

description: Lot number of the sequencing reagent kit used in conjunction with this flow cell. Enables paired traceability between the flow cell consumable and its associated reagent kit for quality investigations, recall management, and GMP compliance. Sourced from LabVantage LIMS run setup records.
reference: GMP 21 CFR Part 211.68; ISO 13485 Section 7.5.8 — Identification and Traceability

description: Date the flow cell was physically received at the Genomics Biotech facility and logged into inventory. Recorded in SAP S/4HANA MM Goods Receipt and LabVantage LIMS. Used to calculate storage duration, validate shelf life, and support FIFO inventory management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Goods Receipt; ISO 13485 Section 7.4.3 — Verification of Purchased Product

description: Regulatory classification of the flow cell indicating its approved use context: RUO (Research Use Only), IVD (In Vitro Diagnostic), LDT (Laboratory Developed Test), or CE-IVD (Conformité Européenne In Vitro Diagnostic). Determines applicable regulatory requirements, labeling obligations, and permissible clinical use. Critical for FDA, EMA, and IVDR compliance.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 809 — In Vitro Diagnostic Products; IVDR EU 2017/746; ISO 13485 Section 7.3

description: Manufacturer-assigned unique serial number printed on the physical flow cell cartridge. Used as the primary external identifier for traceability across LabVantage LIMS, Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub, and SAP S/4HANA inventory management. Enables one-to-one mapping between the physical consumable and its digital record.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.5.8 — Identification and Traceability; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.60

description: Alphanumeric code identifying the physical storage location (e.g., freezer unit, shelf, rack position) where the flow cell is currently stored within the facility. Managed in SAP S/4HANA MM Warehouse Management and LabVantage LIMS. Enables rapid physical retrieval and inventory audits.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Warehouse Management; ISO 13485 Section 6.3 — Infrastructure

description: Maximum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius as specified by the manufacturer. Paired with storage_temperature_min_c to define the acceptable cold chain range. Monitored against environmental monitoring system data to ensure GMP-compliant storage conditions.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.5.11 — Preservation of Product; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.142

description: Minimum required storage temperature in degrees Celsius as specified by the manufacturer. Used to validate cold chain compliance during receipt inspection and ongoing storage monitoring. Deviations from this range trigger quarantine and quality investigation workflows.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.5.11 — Preservation of Product; GMP 21 CFR Part 211.142

business_glossary_term: Supplier Lot Certificate of Analysis (COA) Number
description: Reference number of the Certificate of Analysis (COA) issued by the supplier for this specific lot. The COA documents manufacturer QC test results confirming the flow cell meets specification. Stored in Veeva Vault for regulatory document management and GMP compliance.
reference: GMP 21 CFR Part 211.84; ISO 13485 Section 7.4.3; Veeva Vault Quality Document Management

description: Name of the external supplier or manufacturer who supplied this flow cell (e.g., Illumina, Inc.). Used for procurement lineage, supplier qualification tracking, and quality management. Linked to the reagent and consumable domain for full procurement traceability.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Vendor Master; ISO 13485 Section 7.4 — Purchasing

description: Actual procurement cost per flow cell unit in the operating currency (USD). Sourced from SAP S/4HANA MM invoice verification. Used for Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) allocation, run cost accounting, and financial reporting. Classified as confidential due to commercial sensitivity of supplier pricing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO — Cost Object Controlling; SOX Section 404; GAAP/IFRS Inventory Valuation

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the flow cell master record. Tracks status transitions, QC result updates, and any modifications to the record. Required for data lineage, GxP audit trails, and Silver Layer change tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — Electronic Records; ISO 27001 — Audit Logging; Databricks Delta Lake Change Data Feed

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each sequencing run failure or abort event record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this transactional entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.3 — Control of Nonconforming Product; GxP Deviation Management

description: Reference to the sequencing instrument on which the failed run was executed. Supports instrument reliability tracking, mean time between failures (MTBF) analysis, and preventive maintenance scheduling.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.6 — Control of Monitoring and Measuring Equipment; GxP Equipment Qualification

description: Reference to the laboratory operator or technician who initiated or was responsible for the failed sequencing run. Required for GxP deviation management and operator error root-cause analysis.
reference: CLIA 42 CFR Part 493 — Personnel Requirements; GxP Good Laboratory Practice

description: Reference to the flow cell loaded on the instrument during the failed run. Supports flow cell lot-level failure trending, reagent quality investigation, and consumable reliability analysis.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Flow Cell Object; LabVantage LIMS Consumable Tracking

description: Reference to the sequencing run that experienced the failure or abort event. Links this failure record to the parent run entity for traceability and root-cause analysis.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Object; LabVantage LIMS Run Tracking

description: Foreign key linking to customer.support_case. Business justification: Run failures generate customer support cases for service labs. Links failure events to customer incident tracking, CAPA, rerun coordination, and SLA impact assessment. Essential for customer-facing op

Comma-separated list or range notation of flow cell lane numbers affected by the failure event (e.g., '1,2,3' or '1-4' or 'ALL'). Enables partial-lane failure analysis and assessment of sample impact scope. Null if failure affected the entire flow cell uniformly.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Flow Cell Lane Metrics; NGS Flow Cell Architecture

description: Number of samples whose sequencing data was lost or compromised as a result of this failure event. Drives impact assessment, customer notification decisions, and rerun prioritization. Sourced from the pool/library manifest associated with the failed run.
reference: LabVantage LIMS — Sample Impact Assessment; ISO 15189 Section 5.8 — Reporting of Results

description: The run identifier assigned by Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub for the failed run. Enables direct cross-reference to the BaseSpace run record for diagnostic log retrieval, run metrics review, and support case filing with Illumina.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Object Identifier; NGS Data Management Integration

description: Reference number linking this failure event to a formal Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) record in the quality management system (e.g., Veeva Vault). Null if no formal CAPA was initiated. Supports GxP deviation-to-CAPA traceability.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2 — Corrective Action; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100 — CAPA; Veeva Vault Quality Management

description: Flow cell cluster density (in thousands of clusters per mm²) measured at or near the time of failure. Abnormal cluster density (too high or too low) is a key diagnostic indicator for library preparation issues, loading concentration errors, or flow cell defects.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Cluster Density Metrics; NGS Library Preparation QC Standards

description: Free-text description of the immediate corrective action taken in response to the failure event (e.g., instrument restart, reagent replacement, operator retraining). Distinct from the formal CAPA process; captures the on-the-spot remediation steps.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2 — Corrective Action; GxP Deviation Management; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100

description: Timestamp when this run failure event record was first created in the system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for audit trail and data lineage purposes.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 4.2.5 — Control of Records; GxP Audit Trail Requirements; SOX Section 404

description: Date and time at which the customer or project owner was formally notified of the failure event. Used to measure notification turnaround time (TAT) against SLA commitments and regulatory reporting timelines.
reference: Salesforce CRM — Customer Communication Timestamp; ISO 13485 Section 7.2.3; SLA TAT Measurement

description: Indicates whether the customer or project owner was formally notified of the sequencing run failure and its impact on their samples or data deliverables. Supports SLA compliance tracking and customer communication audit trails.
reference: Salesforce CRM — Customer Communication Log; ISO 13485 Section 7.2.3 — Customer Communication; SLA Management

description: Formal deviation report number assigned in the quality management system (e.g., Veeva Vault) for this failure event. Distinct from the CAPA reference; the deviation report documents the non-conformance event itself, while CAPA tracks the systemic corrective action.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.3 — Control of Nonconforming Product; Veeva Vault Deviation Management; GxP Deviation Reporting

description: Total duration of instrument downtime in minutes attributable to this failure event, from failure detection to instrument return-to-service. Key input for instrument availability KPI calculation, OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) reporting, and maintenance cost analysis.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 7.6 — Equipment Maintenance; GxP Instrument Qualification; OEE Industry Standard

description: Estimated volume of sequencing data (in gigabases, Gb) lost as a result of the failure event. Calculated based on cycles completed, affected lanes, and expected yield per lane. Key metric for assessing business impact and prioritizing rerun decisions. Serves as the QUANTITATIVE_RESULT for this non-monetary transaction.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Yield Metrics; NGS Data Quality Standards

description: High-level classification of the root cause category for the sequencing run failure. Used for trend analysis, quality KPI reporting, and directing corrective action. Categories align with standard GxP deviation classification taxonomy.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; GxP Deviation Classification; FDA 21 CFR Part 820 — Quality System Regulation

description: Structured alphanumeric code identifying the specific failure mode within the failure category. Sourced from the instrument error code library or quality management system codebook (e.g., INS-00142, REA-00031). Enables precise failure mode trending and FMEA alignment.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Instrument Error Codes; ISO 13485 Section 8.3; FMEA Best Practices

description: The sequencing cycle number at which the failure or abort event occurred during the run. Critical for diagnosing instrument or chemistry issues at specific cycle positions (e.g., early cycles vs. late cycles). Null if failure occurred before sequencing commenced.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Cycle Metrics; NGS Run Quality Monitoring

description: Free-text narrative description of the sequencing run failure event, including observed symptoms, error messages, and contextual details captured at the time of detection. Supports root-cause investigation and deviation report authoring.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.3; GxP Deviation Report Content Requirements; Veeva Vault Quality Event Description

description: The precise date and time at which the sequencing run failure or abort event was detected or reported. This is the principal real-world business event timestamp (BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP) for this transaction, distinct from record audit timestamps.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.3; GxP Deviation Management — Event Date/Time Recording

description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for this failure event, used in deviation reports, CAPA references, and quality management system cross-references (e.g., RFE-20240315-0042). Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.3; Veeva Vault Quality Event Numbering; GxP Deviation Management

description: Current lifecycle status of the failure event record within the quality management workflow. Tracks progression from initial detection through investigation, resolution, and closure. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this transaction.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2 — Corrective Action; Veeva Vault Quality Management; GxP Deviation Lifecycle

description: Indicates whether this failure event occurred in a GxP-regulated context (e.g., GMP, GLP, GCP) and therefore requires formal deviation management, CAPA, and regulatory documentation per applicable GxP guidelines. Drives regulatory reporting workflow routing.
reference: GxP Good Practice Regulations; FDA 21 CFR Part 820; ICH Q10; ISO 13485 Section 8.3

description: Verbatim error message or fault code string reported by the sequencing instrument at the time of failure. Sourced directly from instrument logs or Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub run diagnostics. Essential for instrument engineering root-cause analysis.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Instrument Diagnostics Log; GxP Instrument Qualification Records

description: Indicates whether the failed sequencing run was performed as part of an In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD) or Clinical Laboratory Developed Test (LDT) workflow, as opposed to a Research Use Only (RUO) application. Determines applicable regulatory reporting obligations (FDA, IVDR, CLIA).
reference: FDA IVD Regulation 21 CFR Part 809; EU IVDR 2017/746; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; ISO 13485

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Event ID
description: The event or non-conformance record identifier from LabVantage LIMS corresponding to this failure event. Supports bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational LIMS system of record.
reference: LabVantage LIMS — Non-Conformance Event Tracking; ISO 15189 Section 4.9 — Control of Nonconforming Work

description: Additional free-text notes or observations recorded by the investigator, quality team, or instrument engineer during the failure event lifecycle. Captures supplementary context not covered by structured fields, such as environmental conditions, shift notes, or escalation history.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 4.2.5 — Control of Records; GxP Deviation Investigation Notes

description: The mean Phred base quality score (Q-score) recorded at the cycle of failure or at the last completed quality checkpoint before failure. Provides quantitative evidence of data quality degradation leading up to the failure event. Null if failure occurred before quality metrics were generated.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Quality Metrics; NGS Phred Score Standard (Ewing & Green, 1998); ISO 15189

description: Lot number of the sequencing reagent kit used during the failed run. Critical for reagent failure root-cause analysis, lot-level quality investigations, and supplier corrective action requests. Aligns with GMP lot traceability requirements.
reference: GMP 21 CFR Part 211 — Lot Traceability; ISO 13485 Section 7.5.3 — Traceability; SAP S/4HANA MM Batch Management

description: Indicates whether the failed sequencing run must be repeated to recover the lost data or meet the required coverage depth and quality thresholds. Drives rerun scheduling, resource allocation, and customer communication workflows.
reference: LabVantage LIMS — Run Requeue Workflow; NGS Quality Management SOP

description: Date and time at which the failure event was formally resolved and the record was closed in the quality management system. Used to calculate mean time to resolution (MTTR) and compliance with deviation closure SLA targets.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; GxP Deviation Closure Requirements; Veeva Vault Quality Event Closure

description: Confirmed root cause category determined after investigation of the failure event. Distinct from failure_category (which is the initial classification at detection); this field is populated after root-cause analysis is complete. Aligns with standard fishbone/Ishikawa root cause taxonomy.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; ICH Q10 Root Cause Analysis; FDA CAPA Root Cause Classification

description: Detailed narrative of the confirmed root cause identified through formal investigation. Populated after root-cause analysis is completed. Supports CAPA authoring, regulatory submission documentation, and institutional knowledge capture.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.5.2; Veeva Vault Root Cause Analysis Documentation; GxP Investigation Reports

description: Indicates whether a sample quality problem (e.g., degraded DNA, low input concentration, contamination) was identified as a contributing factor to the run failure. Supports sample management quality trending and upstream LIMS feedback.
reference: LabVantage LIMS — Sample QC Flags; ISO 15189 Section 5.4 — Pre-examination Processes

description: Reference to the ServiceNow incident or field service ticket created to manage the instrument repair or technical support response associated with this failure event. Enables cross-system traceability between quality events and IT/field service workflows.
reference: ServiceNow IT Service Management — Incident Management; ISO 13485 Section 7.6 — Equipment Maintenance

description: Severity classification of the failure event based on its impact on data quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and business operations. Drives escalation workflows, notification requirements, and CAPA prioritization.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 8.3; ICH Q10 — Pharmaceutical Quality System; FDA 21 CFR Part 820 — Risk-Based Classification

description: Version of the instrument control software or run control application active at the time of the failure event. Required for software error root-cause analysis and version-specific defect tracking.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Software Version Metadata; GxP Computer System Validation (CSV)

description: The total number of sequencing cycles that were planned for the run at the time of setup. Used in conjunction with failure_cycle to calculate the proportion of the run completed before failure, informing data loss estimation.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Setup Parameters; NGS Read Length Configuration

description: Timestamp when this run failure event record was last modified. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field for audit trail and change tracking purposes.
reference: ISO 13485 Section 4.2.5 — Control of Records; GxP Audit Trail Requirements; SOX Section 404

description: Unique surrogate identifier for a single lane record within a sequencing run on a multi-lane flow cell. Primary key for the run_lane entity. Entity role: TRANSACTION_LINE — represents one lane/line of a sequencing run (TRANSACTION_HEADER), carrying its own QC metrics, yield, and operational state.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; LabVantage LIMS

description: Reference to the sequencing instrument (e.g., NovaSeq 6000, NextSeq 2000) on which this lane was sequenced. Supports instrument utilization tracking, maintenance scheduling, and cross-instrument performance benchmarking.
reference: LabVantage LIMS; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

description: Reference to the laboratory operator or scientist responsible for loading and initiating the sequencing run for this lane. Supports GxP audit trail requirements, operator performance tracking, and training compliance verification. Satisfies TRANSACTION_LINE category: PARTY_REFERENCE (via the parent run, but captured at lane level for traceability).
reference: GxP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 15189; MasterControl; Oracle Cloud HCM

description: Reference to the physical flow cell consumable loaded on the instrument for this run. Links lane-level performance data to the specific flow cell lot and type (e.g., NovaSeq 6000 S4 flow cell). Satisfies TRANSACTION_LINE category: RESOURCE_REFERENCE.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: Foreign key linking to reference.genome_assembly. Business justification: Lane-level QC metrics (alignment rate, on-target percentage) require reference genome specification. Critical for lane-level quality assessment and troubleshooting in production sequencing operations.

Reference to the multiplexed library pool or individual library loaded onto this lane. Enables traceability from lane-level sequencing output back to the sample preparation and library construction records in the LIMS.
reference: LabVantage LIMS; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

description: Reference to the parent sequencing run (TRANSACTION_HEADER) that this lane belongs to. Satisfies TRANSACTION_LINE category: HEADER_REFERENCE — the lane is a line-level record within the run.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; LabVantage LIMS

description: Name and version of the base calling software used to convert raw intensity signals to nucleotide sequences (FASTQ) for this lane (e.g., Illumina RTA 3.4.4, DRAGEN). Critical for data provenance, reproducibility, and regulatory traceability of genomic data.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; GxP; ISO 15189; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

description: Version identifier of the base calling software used for this lane. Required for GxP audit trails and bioinformatics reproducibility; version changes may affect base quality scores and downstream variant calling results.
reference: GxP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ISO 15189; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

description: Unique identifier for this lane as recorded in Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub, the primary system of record for sequencing data management. Enables direct linkage between the enterprise data lakehouse and the BaseSpace platform for data retrieval and audit.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; GxP; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

description: Percentage of clusters that pass Illumina's chastity filter, indicating the proportion of high-quality reads retained after filtering. A key run-level QC metric; typically ≥75–85% is expected for acceptable run quality. Sourced from Illumina InterOp.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; ISO 15189; CLIA

description: Percentage of target bases covered at ≥20% of the mean coverage depth, measuring how evenly reads are distributed across the target region. High uniformity indicates consistent library preparation and sequencing performance. Sourced from Picard or samtools.

Date and time when this QC metric record was first created in the system, typically upon automated ingestion from the source QC tool (InterOp, BaseSpace, Picard, or samtools). Supports audit trail requirements under GxP and FDA 21 CFR Part 11.

Percentage of reads identified as PCR or optical duplicates, which are removed prior to variant calling. High duplication rates reduce effective coverage and indicate over-amplification during library preparation. Sourced from Picard MarkDuplicates.

Percentage of base calls that do not match the reference sequence, typically measured using PhiX control spike-in. Reflects sequencing chemistry and instrument performance. Lower values indicate higher accuracy. Sourced from Illumina InterOp.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; ISO 15189; CLIA

description: Quantitative measure of GC content bias in sequencing coverage, indicating the degree to which GC-rich or GC-poor regions are over- or under-represented relative to expected coverage. Values near 0 indicate minimal bias. Sourced from Picard CollectGcBiasMetrics.

Standard deviation of the insert size distribution in base pairs. High standard deviation indicates heterogeneous fragmentation, which can affect alignment accuracy and coverage uniformity. Sourced from Picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics.

Average number of times each base in the target region (genome, exome, or panel) is covered by sequencing reads, expressed as fold-coverage (X). Primary metric for assessing whether sufficient sequencing depth was achieved for reliable variant calling. Populated for library-level records. Sourced from Picard or samtools.

Average size of the DNA fragment inserted between sequencing adapters, in base pairs. Reflects library preparation quality; deviations from expected insert size indicate degradation, over-fragmentation, or adapter contamination. Sourced from Picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics.

Average Phred quality score across all bases in the run or lane, representing overall base call accuracy. A Phred score of 30 corresponds to 99.9% accuracy. Used for instrument performance benchmarking and run-level QC trending.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; ISO 15189; CLIA

description: Median fold-coverage across the target region, less sensitive to outliers than mean coverage. Used alongside mean_coverage_depth to assess coverage uniformity and detect regions of extreme over- or under-representation. Sourced from Picard or samtools.

Indicates the level of aggregation at which this QC metric record applies: 'run' for instrument-wide metrics, 'lane' for per-lane flow cell metrics, or 'library' for per-library/per-sample coverage metrics. Determines which metric fields are populated and how the record is used in QC workflows.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub; bcl2fastq; ISO 15189

description: Identifies the upstream tool or system from which this QC metric record was derived: Illumina InterOp files, BaseSpace, bcl2fastq demultiplexing stats, Picard alignment tools, samtools, DRAGEN, or other. description: Percentage of aligned reads that map to the intended target region (exome capture or targeted panel). Applicable for WES and targeted sequencing assays. Low on-target rates indicate poor library enrichment or capture efficiency. Sourced from Picard CollectHsMetrics.

Fraction of target bases covered at a minimum depth of 100X, expressed as a percentage. Used for high-depth targeted sequencing panels, somatic variant calling, and liquid biopsy applications requiring high sensitivity at low allele frequencies. Sourced from Picard or samtools.

Fraction of target bases covered at a minimum depth of 10X, expressed as a percentage. Used as a coverage adequacy threshold for low-depth applications and as a QC gate for variant calling sensitivity. Sourced from Picard CollectHsMetrics or samtools depth.

Fraction of target bases covered at a minimum depth of 20X, expressed as a percentage. Standard coverage threshold for WES clinical assays; used to assess whether sufficient depth was achieved for reliable heterozygous variant detection. Sourced from Picard or samtools.

Fraction of target bases covered at a minimum depth of 30X, expressed as a percentage. Common coverage threshold for WGS clinical applications; used to confirm adequate depth for high-confidence variant calling across the genome. Sourced from Picard or samtools.

Number of reads passing Illumina's chastity filter (PF reads), representing high-quality reads used in downstream alignment and variant calling. Distinct from total_reads which includes all raw clusters. Sourced from Illumina InterOp or bcl2fastq.

description: Percentage of clusters that pass the Illumina chastity filter (PF = Passing Filter), indicating the proportion of reads with sufficient signal purity for reliable base calling. A key run-level QC metric; typically expected to be >75-80% for a passing run.
reference: Illumina Quality Metrics Documentation; CAP NGS Checklist NGS.40100; ISO 20166

description: Date and time when this sequencing run record was first created in the enterprise data system (LIMS or BaseSpace ingestion). reference: GxP 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; ISO 27001 Audit Logging; SOX Section 404

description: Data retention classification for this sequencing run record and its associated FASTQ/BAM/VCF outputs, determining the minimum retention period per applicable regulations. 'standard' = 2 years (RUO); 'extended' = 10+ years (clinical/GxP); 'permanent' = indefinite (regulatory submission data); 'restricted_deletion' = deletion requires regulatory approval.
reference: HIPAA §164.530(j) Record Retention; CLIA §493.1105; FDA 21 CFR §211.180; GDPR Article 5(1)(e); NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

description: Current status of the FASTQ demultiplexing process for this run, which separates pooled (multiplexed) sample reads by their index barcodes into individual sample FASTQ files. Tracks the post-run data processing step that precedes bioinformatics pipeline execution.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — DRAGEN Demultiplexing; Illumina bcl2fastq Documentation

description: Date and time when the sequencing run completed (final cycle finished or run terminated). Used with run_start_timestamp to calculate run duration and TAT. Null if run is still in progress or queued. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run End Time; LabVantage LIMS

description: The base-level sequencing error rate for this run expressed as a percentage, calculated using PhiX control spike-in alignment. Lower values indicate higher sequencing accuracy. Used for run QC acceptance/rejection decisions and instrument performance trending.
reference: Illumina PhiX Control Library; Illumina BaseSpace Run Metrics; CAP NGS Checklist NGS.40200

description: The storage path or URI (e.g., S3 bucket path, BaseSpace project URL, or HPC filesystem path) where the FASTQ output files for this run are stored. Confidential as it reveals internal data infrastructure topology. Used by bioinformatics pipelines to locate raw sequencing data.
reference: ISO 27001 Information Security; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; HIPAA §164.312 Technical Safeguards

description: The type/format of flow cell used in this run (e.g., SP, S1, S2, S4 for NovaSeq; P1, P2, P3 for NovaSeq X; nano, micro for MiSeq). reference: Illumina Instrument Run Folder Naming Convention; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

description: Number of base pairs sequenced for the index (barcode) reads used in multiplexing/demultiplexing. Typically 6, 8, or 10 bp per index. Determines the number of samples that can be multiplexed on a single flow cell and the accuracy of demultiplexing.
reference: Illumina Multiplexing Guidelines; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Parameters

description: The specific Illumina instrument platform model used for this sequencing run. Captured at run time for performance benchmarking, platform-specific QC thresholds, and bioinformatics pipeline configuration. description: Indicates whether this run was configured as paired-end (True) or single-read (False) sequencing. Paired-end sequencing generates reads from both ends of a DNA fragment, improving alignment accuracy and variant detection. Critical parameter for bioinformatics pipeline configuration.
reference: Illumina Paired-End Sequencing Technology; NGS Library Preparation Best Practices

description: Number of lanes on the flow cell used in this sequencing run (e.g., 1 for MiSeq, 2 for NextSeq, 4 for NovaSeq SP/S1/S2, 8 for NovaSeq S4). Used for per-lane QC analysis, sample distribution planning, and run capacity calculations.
reference: Illumina Flow Cell Architecture Documentation; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Lane Metrics

description: Name or catalog identifier of the library preparation kit used to prepare samples for this sequencing run (e.g., 'Illumina DNA Prep', 'TruSeq Stranded mRNA', 'Nextera DNA Flex'). Affects sequencing performance, adapter trimming parameters, and bioinformatics pipeline configuration.
reference: Illumina Library Preparation Kit Catalog; LabVantage LIMS — Protocol Management; ISO 13485 §7.5

description: Free-text field for operator or QC reviewer notes about this sequencing run, including observations about run performance, deviations from SOP, troubleshooting actions taken, or contextual information relevant to data interpretation. Supports GxP deviation documentation.
reference: GxP SOP Documentation Requirements; CLIA §493.1291; ISO 15189 §5.8

description: Total sequencing data output generated by this run measured in gigabases (Gb). Represents the QUANTITATIVE_RESULT for this non-monetary TRANSACTION_HEADER. Used for run performance benchmarking, storage capacity planning, and comparison against instrument specifications.
reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Metrics; Illumina Instrument Specification Sheets

description: Percentage of PhiX bacteriophage control library spiked into the sequencing run for real-time quality monitoring and error rate calibration. Typically 1-5% for standard runs. Used to calculate error_rate_pct and validate instrument performance.
reference: Illumina PhiX Control v3 Library Documentation; CAP NGS Checklist

description: Number of samples planned to be multiplexed and sequenced in this run as defined in the sample sheet at run setup. Used for capacity planning, reagent consumption estimation, and comparison against actual demultiplexed sample count.
reference: Illumina Sample Sheet Specification; LabVantage LIMS — Run Planning

description: Percentage of bases with a Phred quality score of 30 or higher (Q30), indicating ≥99.9% base call accuracy. The primary industry-standard run quality metric. Typically required to be >75-80% for a run to pass QC. Directly impacts variant calling accuracy and clinical reporting confidence.
reference: Phred Quality Score Standard (Ewing & Green 1998); CAP NGS Checklist; CLIA §493.1253; Illumina BaseSpace Run Metrics

description: Date and time when the QC review of this sequencing run was completed and the run_qc_status was formally assigned. Part of the GxP electronic audit trail. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

The overall QC pass/fail determination for this sequencing run based on evaluation of run metrics (Q30%, cluster density, error rate, yield). 'pass' = all metrics within specification; 'fail' = one or more critical metrics out of specification; 'pending_review' = awaiting manual QC review; 'conditional_pass' = passed with noted deviations. Determines whether downstream FASTQ data is released for analysis.
reference: CAP NGS Checklist; CLIA §493.1253; ISO 15189 §5.6; GxP QC Release Procedures

description: The number of base pairs sequenced per read in this run (e.g., 75, 100, 150, 250 bp). A key sequencing parameter that determines data quality, coverage, and application suitability. Configured at run setup and recorded for QC and reproducibility.
reference: Illumina Sequencing by Synthesis Technology; NGS Best Practices; ISO 20166 Molecular In Vitro Diagnostic Examinations

description: Regulatory classification of this sequencing run's intended use. IVD = In Vitro Diagnostic (FDA/IVDR regulated); RUO = Research Use Only (not for clinical use); LDT = Laboratory Developed Test (CLIA-regulated); GMP/GLP/GCP = applicable Good Practice framework. Determines data handling, retention, and reporting obligations.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 820 IVD Regulations; IVDR 2017/746; CLIA 42 CFR §493; GxP Regulations

description: The NGS application type or sequencing strategy for this run. Determines the library preparation approach, bioinformatics pipeline, and downstream analysis. WGS = Whole Genome Sequencing; WES = Whole Exome Sequencing; targeted = targeted panel sequencing; amplicon = amplicon-based sequencing; RNA-seq = transcriptome sequencing; metagenomics = environmental/microbial sequencing.
reference: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; Illumina Application Notes; IVDR 2017/746 Annex I

description: Human-readable name assigned to the sequencing run, typically following a lab naming convention (e.g., 'RUN-2024-001-NovaSeq'). Used for identification in LIMS, BaseSpace, and operational dashboards. Maps to the Run Name field in Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub.

reference: Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub — Run Status Enumeration; LabVantage LIMS Workflow States

description: Classification of the run by its intended use context. 'clinical' = IVD/LDT clinical diagnostic run subject to CLIA/CAP; 'research' = RUO research run; 'validation' = assay validation run; 'QC' = quality control run; 'development' = R&D development run. description: Total number of sequencing chemistry cycles executed in this run. For paired-end runs, this includes both read 1, index reads, and read 2 cycles (e.g., 2×150 bp = 300 cycles + index cycles). Used for run cost accounting, reagent consumption tracking, and run configuration validation.
